TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression on a 3 Tesla scanner.

FINDINGS
A sizable, approximately 1.5 cm osteochondral loose body is observed in the medial recess of the joint cavity. The lesion has detached from the medial facet of the mid-portion of the patella, which has Wiberg II morphology. The opposing femoral trochlea is congenitally shallow (Sulcus angle 173°). A small joint effusion is noted in the knee joint. The cruciate and collateral ligaments appear within normal limits. The menisci do not show pathological findings. The articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartments is normal. A small area of edema on the deep aspect of the iliotibial band at the level of the lateral femoral epicondyle could represent iliotibial band friction syndrome. Satisfactory healing is noted following repair of the quadriceps tendon.

CONCLUSION
Osteochondral loose body in the medial parapatellar recess of the joint, detached from the patella.

Medial degenerative lesions.

Cruciate ligaments intact, and collateral ligaments of preserved thickness and signal.
The lateral meniscus shows diffuse fibrillation of its free edge, with intrasubstance signal alteration of the anterior horn of degenerative nature.
Moderate extrusion of the medial meniscus, with radial tear of the inner two-thirds of the posterior horn. Complex tear of the body region, with free edge fibrillation, an oblique vertical component and a horizontal component, causing displacement of meniscal tissue into the meniscotibial recess. Moderate parameniscal edema.
Diffuse superficial irregularity of the cartilage of the lateral femorotibial compartment.
Moderate cartilage thinning with full-thickness ulcers in the central region and medial facet of the patella. Diffuse superficial irregularity of the trochlear cartilage, with moderate thickness thinning on the medial slope.

Thickening and increased signal of the medial patellar plica, extending over the medial slope of the trochlea.

Quadriceps, patellar, popliteus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris, iliotibial band, and pes anserine tendons of preserved thickness and signal.
Muscle groups of preserved trophism and signal.

Nearly complete radial tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with moderate meniscal extrusion, associated with a complex tear of the body region and displacement of meniscal tissue into the meniscotibial recess.
Degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus, with diffuse free edge fibrillation.
Diffuse grade 4 medial femorotibial chondropathy, with regional bone edema suggestive of overload phenomena.
Grade 2 lateral femorotibial chondropathy. Grade 3-4 patellar chondropathy and grade 2-3 trochlear chondropathy. Mild to moderate joint effusion, with mild diffuse synovitis.
Thickening and increased signal of the medial patellar plica.

LEFT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is extruded 3.5 mm medially in the knee joint. Volume loss is present in the meniscus, and grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Diffuse thickening and increased signal secondary to mucoid degeneration are observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. Signal change consistent with medullary bone marrow edema is observed at the tibial intercondylar eminence at the level of the anterior cruciate ligament attachment. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral millimetric cysts and edema are observed in the medial femoral condyle adjacent to the joint. Thinning and destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage are observed at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Volume loss, medial extrusion, and grade III meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus. Mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. Bone marrow edema at the tibial intercondylar eminence. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Patient reports history of chondroblastoma to the right knee diagnosed in <[YEAR]> but not fully worked up. X-ray in <[Month]> <[YEAR]> confirms nonspecific lytic lesion right patella. Please assess.

PRIOR IMAGING: Plain film radiographs from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

In the superolateral aspect of the patella there is a T2 bright focus with irregular sclerotic margination seen on the plain film characterized by low signal margination on MRI. This focal lesion has central T2 bright signal similar in signal to articular cartilage and has a linear cartilaginous signal extending posteriorly to the articular surface of patella. The articular cartilage of patella directly posterior to this focus is intact but does demonstrate slight contour irregularity and signal change which may represent mild chondrosis. The finding measures about 1 cm in maximum diameter. The appearance is typical in location and MRI features of a dorsal defect of the patella. This represents a normal anatomic variant.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The TT-TG distance measures about 1.5 cm, at the upper limits of normal, consistent with an element of mild lateralization of the tibial tubercle

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

Within the lateral femoral condyle there is a serpiginously marginated lesion measuring 2.1 AP, 1.4 cm with an 0.9 cm in depth situated 2 to 3 mm deep to the cortex of the lateral femoral condyle. The rim of this lesion is T2 bright and T1 dark with central fat. MR features are typical of a bone infarct. No evidence of cortical collapse.

The medial meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a trace Baker's cyst demonstrated. No significant knee effusion is demonstrated.

A few small subcentimeter popliteal lymph nodes are incidentally noted.

Marrow signal is otherwise normal. No other bone infarcts are seen within field-of-view.

INTERPRETATION: 
Subcortical chondroid focus in the superolateral aspect of patella has MR features typical of a dorsal defect of the patella. The finding is not typical of a chondroblastoma. Mild overlying chondromalacia patella.

Mild lateralization of tibial tubercle.

Trace Baker's cyst.

There is a bone infarct seen in the lateral femoral condyle. No evidence of articular collapse.
Clinical correlation as to the possible cause of a bone infarct in this patient is recommended.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
In the medial compartment, a degenerative tear of the meniscus is observed with reduced meniscal mass (it is not known whether prior arthroscopy has been performed). Additionally, there are coexisting congruent lesions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss on the femoral and tibial condyles (ICRS grade IV), while further foci of bone marrow edema are observed subchondrally in the medial femoral condyle and over a large extent in the metaphysis of the medial tibial condyle. Overall, the findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis with a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture of the medial proximal tibia.

In the lateral compartment, no significant pathological findings are observed.

On evaluation of the anterior compartment, satisfactory congruence of the patella and trochlea is observed, which however appears congenitally shallow. The anterior cruciate ligament shows myxoid degeneration. The posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments appear within normal limits. Intra-articularly, a moderate fluid collection is observed.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] male complaining of left knee pain and swelling. Ultrasound shows focal tear of the lateral collateral ligament versus ligament sprain and likely tear of the medial and lateral meniscus. Joint effusion in the suprapatellar recess and Baker's cyst. Recommended by radiologist.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is mild thickening and increased T2 signal in the proximal fibers of the patellar tendon. Findings are consistent with mild patellar tendinosis. Quadriceps and patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable.

The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint demonstrates mild chondral fraying at the patellar apex and also within the femoral trochlea but overall cartilage is reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is mild non-surfacing signal seen in the posterior horn of medial meniscus peripherally. Involving posterior horn near the posterior root attachment of medial meniscus there is mild apical truncation and fraying of the meniscus consistent with a subtle radial tear. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment demonstrates regions of chondral fraying and thinning with a few subcortical cysts seen within the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle in keeping with moderate chondrosis.

There is a subtle tear in the lateral meniscus involving anterior horn and anterior body in keeping with the radial tear in this region. There is also a horizontal signal in keeping with a horizontal tear extending into the anterior horn of lateral meniscus. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment demonstrates chondral fraying and thinning but is reasonably well-maintained. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis. Minimal degenerative spurring to the lateral joint compartment is noted.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, the fibular collateral ligament, the biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a small Baker's cyst. There is edema and fluid seen around the pes anserine tendons consistent with pes anserine bursitis.

There is a small knee effusion. Mild reactive synovitis is noted.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Mild tricompartmental chondrosis with early degenerative spurring to the lateral joint margin.

Subtle meniscal tears to the lateral and medial menisci as described.

Small Baker's cyst.

Pes anserine bursitis.

Background changes of lateralization of the tibial tubercle and shallowness of the trochlear groove predisposing to patellar dislocation.

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1-weighted pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

RIGHT KNEE
The cruciate and collateral ligaments appear within normal limits. Intra-articular fluid collection is observed in communication with a large Baker's synovial cyst, craniocaudal diameter 7.5 cm. The bone marrow presents benign hyperplasia. In the lateral compartment of the knee, degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with severe erosion of the articular cartilage of the femoral condyle and the tibia, ICRS STAGE III. There is coexisting degenerative tear of the meniscus and presence of marginal osteophytes and a small focus of subarticular bone marrow edema in the medial tibial epicondyle. On evaluation of the medial compartment, only subtle degenerative changes are observed with small marginal osteophytes and fissural erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle. On evaluation of the anterior (patellofemoral) compartment, findings of degenerative osteoarthritis are observed with erosion of the articular cartilage of the lateral articular surface ICRS STAGE II and of the medial articular surface ICRS STAGE IV. The patella has Wiberg II morphology and in combination with the shallow trochlea predisposes to tracking dysfunction. There is coexisting prepatellar bursitis.

Small ganglion cysts are observed posteriorly along the distal metaphysis-diaphysis of the femur.

Findings of degenerative osteoarthritis, particularly in the medial compartment, with associated synovitis and development of lipoma arborescens.

Gonarthrotic changes are present with formation of periarticular osteophytes, as well as sharpening of the intercondylar eminences. The cartilage covering the femur and tibia on the medial side appears thinned. The cartilage covering the articular surfaces of the patella is of homogeneous structure and signal intensity. MRI findings of rupture of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extrusion of approximately 3.5 mm. The signal intensity of the lateral meniscus is also increased in its anterior and posterior horns, as in advanced degenerative changes. A multiloculated cyst is depicted in association with the damaged meniscus. A loose body is visualized immediately behind the posterior cruciate ligament. Three similar findings are visualized, located adjacent to the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, as well as above the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Correlation with radiographic imaging of the knee joint is desirable. Both cruciate ligaments are traced to their attachment sites with normal shape and signal intensity. Both collateral ligaments are of normal shape, homogeneous structure and signal intensity to their attachment sites. MRI findings of a small joint effusion. The patella is of Wiberg type I. Insall-Salvati ratio: 1.25.

Conclusion: Rupture of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extrusion. Degeneratively changed lateral meniscus. Intra-articular loose bodies. Gonarthrotic changes grade II according to the Kellgren and Lawrence classification. Small joint effusion.

Clinical History:
Medial meniscal injury, right knee.

Findings:
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, with no signs of tear.
Complex tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with a segment partially displaced into the posterior intercondylar region and meniscal extrusion at the level of the body. Edema of the regional soft tissues and peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial tibial plateau, likely reactive.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the weight-bearing zone of the femorotibial compartments, predominantly medial. Trochlear cartilage without alterations. Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the patellar cartilage with diffuse distribution.
Mild joint effusion with mild synovitis. Popliteal cyst with probable caudal leakage.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, with no signs of tear.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Complex tear of the medial meniscus with displaced segments, as previously described. Peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial tibial plateau, reactive to the adjacent soft tissues.
Chondropathy with grade 2 lesions of the femorotibial compartments, predominantly medial.
Chondropathy with grade 2 lesions of the patella.
Mild joint effusion with mild synovitis. Popliteal cyst with probable leakage.
Mild proximal patellar tendinosis and distal quadriceps tendinosis.

* Increased infiltration in the muscle of popliteus muscle and intermuscular infiltration(srs:[ID], Img:24; srs:6001, Img:26), R/O mild myositis

2. Status of lateral subluxation of patella, R/O grade 2 injury of medial patellar retinaculum.
3. High riding patella in this study but no significant evidence of full thickness tear of patellar tendon.
4. In favor of grade 1 patellar chondromalacia.
5. R/O mild myositis of popliteus muscle.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

MRI findings: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the knee joint have preserved shape and signal characteristics. Three bone lesions are seen, two of which are located in the lateral femoral condyle and one in the tibial epiphysis, to the left of the midline. They show low signal intensity on T1-weighted sequences. On PDW SPAIR sequences, the lesion located anteriorly in the lateral femoral condyle is entirely of low signal intensity, while the other two have a hyperintense center and hypointense periphery. The described lesions measure 4.7/2.5 mm, 5.0/4.0 mm, and 7.0/4.5 mm. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia has preserved thickness and congruence.
Patella, patellar cartilage – unremarkable. No MRI evidence of degenerative or traumatic changes in the anterior and posterior horns of both menisci. Normal appearance of the cruciate ligaments. Collateral ligaments – normal appearance. Patellar retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon – preserved thickness and signal characteristics. Patellar ligament – a focal area of increased signal intensity is seen on PDW SPAIR sequences measuring 9/5 mm, located at the insertion site of the ligament at the inferior pole of the patella. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. Conclusion: MRI findings consistent with patellar tendinosis ("Jumper's knee"). The bone lesions located in the tibia and femur most likely correspond to compact bone islands.

The MRI of right knee without IV adminstration of contrast medium is performed with the pulse sequences - sagittal T1, PD+FS, and T2+FS, axial T2+FS and coronal T2+FS. 

The MR images reveal: 

> Osteoarthric change of right knee. Grossly preserved joint space and alignment. 
> PD hyperintensities are detected in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. More in favor of medial meniscus degenerative tear.
> Presence of PD hyperintensities in the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), probably secondary to the posttraumatic injury or chronic inflammation. 
> Subchondral erosions, subcortical cysts, and cartilage thinning at the lateral patellofemoral joint. Osteoarthritis and advanced chondromalacia is favored. 
> The continuity and alignment of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) are preserved. 
> Normal joint effusion. 
> The lateral meniscus is intact without tear. 
> Presence of some fluid collection in the infrapatellar bursa. 
> Presence of a small hyperintensity in the upper portion of the patella, reflecting a focal tendinitis. 
> Subcutaneous edematous infiltration is detected at anterior knee. In favor of inflammation. 
> The medial and lateral collateral ligaments, iliotibial tract, quadriceps tendon, and other structures are intact without definite abnormalities by this knee MR examination. 

<Impressions> : 
1) Osteoarthric change of right knee. 
2) PD hyperintensities are detected in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. More in favor of medial meniscus degenerative tear. 
3) Presence of PD hyperintensities in the posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), probably secondary to the posttraumatic injury or chronic inflammation. 
4) Subchondral erosions, subcortical cysts, and cartilage thinning at the lateral patellofemoral joint. Osteoarthritis and advanced chondromalacia is favored. 
5) Presence of some fluid collection in the infrapatellar bursa. 
6) Presence of a small hyperintensity in the upper portion of the patella, reflecting a focal tendinitis.
[ID]. In favor of inflammation. 

Recommend clinical correlation and Orthopedics consultation for further evaluation and management.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
No pathological findings are observed on evaluation of the medial and lateral compartments, including the menisci.
In the region of the tibial epiphysis, particularly lateral to the midline, there are confluent small cystic lesions with a total transverse diameter of 2.5 cm with surrounding edema.
The cruciate and collateral ligaments have normal morphology.
On evaluation of the anterior compartment and the extensor mechanism, there is degeneration of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade 4) at the inferior lateral aspect of the patella with lateral subluxation of the patella and signs of impingement of the patellar tendon on the lateral femoral condyle with edema in the parapatellar fat pad.
Intra-articularly, there is a fluid collection with the presence of small loose bodies in the lateral parapatellar recess.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the patellofemoral joint.
2. Joint effusion and small loose bodies with features of early chondromatosis secondary to osteoarthritis.
3. The cystic lesions in the tibial epiphysis could represent either confluent small intraosseous ganglion cysts or subarticular degenerative cysts.
4. Findings of impingement syndrome of the lateral patellar tendon on the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

MRI findings: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. A minimal amount of fluid is seen behind the patellar cartilage. The bones forming the knee joint are of normal shape and signal intensity. A degenerative bone cyst is seen medially in the tibial epiphysis. It measures 14/11 mm and has heterogeneous signal characteristics. Marginal osteophytes are present on the lateral condyles of the tibia and femur. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia is severely thinned to absent, with loss of congruence. Subchondral osteosclerosis of the lateral tibial plateau in the setting of the described cartilage defect. Isolated subcortical osteosclerotic changes are also present cortically along the lateral femoral condyle. The lateral meniscus, at the level of the described changes, is ruptured and completely extruded laterally. Within it, a meniscal cyst measuring 16/10 mm is seen in the intercondylar region. Degenerative changes are present in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. MRI evidence of complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. It is thickened predominantly in its distal third near the tibial insertion. The ligament shows increased signal intensity. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patella with an osteophyte along the inferior posterior margin. Retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – unremarkable. Normal appearance of the soft tissues and the intercondylar fossa.

Conclusion: MRI evidence of gonarthrotic changes of the right knee joint. Chondropathy with lysis of the cartilage of the tibia and femur on the lateral side of the joint. Rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Complete rupture with extrusion of the lateral meniscus. Osteosclerotic changes of the adjacent articular surfaces laterally. Degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.

text: MRI findings: MRI evidence of joint effusion. Free fluid is visualized in the suprapatellar recess, as well as in the recess of the posterior cruciate ligament. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur on the lateral side of the knee joint is of preserved thickness and congruence. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side of the joint is thinned in its outermost third. Osteophytes have formed along the medial and lateral articular margins of the femur and tibia, along the anterior and posterior surfaces of the femoral condyles, as well as along the superior pole of the patella. Normal MRI appearance of both menisci. The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact. MRI evidence of partial tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral insertion. The ligament is of increased diameter and increased signal intensity over a length of approximately 8 mm. Medial collateral ligament, patellar retinacula – unremarkable. The cartilage of the femur in the patellofemoral joint is also irregularly thinned, with small edema zones seen in the underlying femur. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – normal appearance. A fabella measuring 7/4 mm is visualized. [DATE]: MRI Left Knee 15ch

Clinical information: Medial gonalgia, therapy-resistant.
Diagnostic question: Subchondral insufficiency fracture, avascular necrosis?

Findings:
Advanced medial femorotibial cartilage disease with complete loss of cartilage of the medial half of the weight-bearing portion of the medial condyle and tibial plateau, accompanied by subchondral edema bilaterally without underlying necrosis or insufficiency fracture.
Markedly degenerative appearance of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, nearly equivalent to a transfixing radial tear, unstable.
Mildly thickened appearance of the anterior cruciate ligament, with mildly increased T2 signal: mucoid degeneration.
Voluminous joint effusion, with multiple loose bodies in the posterior lateral compartment.

Early gonarthrosis of the left knee,
- Predominantly medial femorotibial compartment,
- With significant cartilage loss predominantly in the medial weight-bearing portion of the medial femorotibial compartment, and markedly degenerative appearance of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (equivalent of a transfixing radial tear),
- With subchondral bone edema of the tibial plateau and femoral condyle,
- Currently with voluminous joint effusion and several loose bodies posteriorly.

The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

Intra-articularly, a joint effusion is observed in communication with a small Baker's cyst, which demonstrates focal synovitis, as well as presence of multiple cartilaginous loose bodies (synovial chondromatosis).

In the superior medial portion of Hoffa's fat pad, edema is observed representing mild impingement syndrome.

In keeping with the provided history there is a bucket-handle tear of the lateral meniscus. The body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus are diminutive and there is a large flipped fragment demonstrated within the intercondylar notch passing anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. Linear signal also extends into the anterior horn of lateral meniscus consistent with extension of the tear to the anterior horn.

There is an associated osteochondral injury seen to the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. In this region there is mild contour flattening of the articular surface of the posterior aspect of lateral femoral condyle associated with regions of focal cartilage fraying and articular cartilage loss. There is edema seen within the lateral femoral condyle in association with this finding in keeping with resolving bone contusion. Small marginal osteophytes are seen to the lateral joint compartment consistent with early osteoarthritic change.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and appear unremarkable. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained. Minimal degenerative spurring is seen at the articular surfaces of the patellofemoral joint. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits measuring about 8 mm.

The examination was performed with T1-weighted pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

In the medial femoral condyle, a concavity of the weight-bearing portion of the condyle is visible, approximately 16 mm in diameter, with pronounced bone edema. Delamination with multifragmentary fracture of the cartilage of the medial femoral condyle with free cartilaginous joint bodies. The described findings are consistent with a subchondral insufficiency fracture (SONK, Ahlbäck disease).
Zones of bone edema of the medial tibial condyle and subcortically in the region of the lateral femoral condyle.
Focal zones of denudation and grade 4 chondromalacia of the femorotibial joint.
Early degenerative changes of the femoropatellar joint with osteophytes and cartilage thinning, and grade 1–2 chondromalacia of the patellar facet cartilage.
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament, without signs of rupture.
The posterior cruciate ligament has appropriate signal intensity, without signs of rupture.
Severe degenerative changes of the medial meniscus with complex tear of the body and posterior horn with meniscal extrusion. Consequent distension of the medial collateral ligament, without signs of rupture.
Moderate degenerative changes of the lateral meniscus, without signs of rupture.
Enthesopathic changes of the proximal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament.
Enthesopathic changes and bursitis of the popliteus tendon.
Normal appearance of the iliotibial tract and pes anserinus.
Enthesopathic changes of the insertion of the quadriceps tendon and the tibial insertion of the patellar ligament.
Distension of both patellar retinacula.
Moderate amount of joint effusion, most pronounced suprapatellarly. Thickened complete suprapatellar plica.
Edema of the subcutaneous fat tissue.
In the distal third of the thigh, in the anterior subcutaneous fat tissue, a lipoma measuring approximately 26x16 mm.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

Interruption of the quadriceps tendon with retraction of proximal tendon and increased interstitial signal intensity, reflecting tear.
Increased joint effusion with heterogeous signal intensity of internal content and suprapatellar bursitis with hypertrophy of the synovium and extending the joint effusion to prepatellar region via quadriceps tendon gap and in favor of involving prepatellar bursa and lateral popliteal foass..
Diffuse subcutaneous edema and muscle edema  around knee to distal thigh and increased intermuscular fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation, R/O cellulitis, myositis and fasciitis.
Ill-defined bone marrow edema in distal femur, proximal tibia and patella, R/O osteomyelitis or bone marrow inflamamtion.
Laxity of patellar tendon.
> The contour of ACL is in a straight line but increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.

Impression: 
1. Quadriceps tendon rupture.
2. R/O septic arthrtis of right knee with massive joint effusion, suprapatellar and prepatellar bursitis and adjacent osteomyelitis;  differential diagnosis of gouty arthritis or inflammatory arthritis with adjacent bone marrow inflammation.
3. R/O cellulitis, fasciitis and myositis over distal thigh to proximal leg.
4. R/O grade 1 injury of ACL.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and lab data and artherocentesis for further evaluation

Minor bone stress changes in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial condyle however no discrete fracture. Intact lateral meniscus.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Focal high-grade chondral fissuring along the lateral femoral trochlear surface with minor underlying bone stress change. Otherwise well-maintained tricompartmental hyaline cartilage.  
Conclusion: On a background of mucoid degeneration there is a complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with an associated 13 mm 16 mm x 7 mm parameniscal cyst posteriorly. Minor bone stress changes in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial condyle however no discrete fracture. Ancillary findings described above.

text: MRI findings: The bones forming the left knee joint are of normal shape, structure, and signal intensity. No evidence of joint effusion. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur is preserved. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is torn. Along the entire length of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, a thick hyperintense lesion with oblique course is seen, reaching the edge of the meniscus. Medial to the meniscus, a large multiloculated cystic lesion is seen, which is associated with the torn medial meniscus. The cyst measures approximately 44/26 mm in overall size. Lateral meniscus and anterior horn of the medial meniscus – unremarkable. Anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments – normal appearance. At the distal end of the patellar ligament, a rounded bony structure measuring 11 mm is seen. The shape of the tibial tuberosity is altered with a bony defect. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Retinacula – unremarkable. Patellar cartilage, patella – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon – unremarkable. No changes are seen in the soft tissues of the left knee. Conclusion: MRI findings of injury to the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 3 with meniscal cyst. The changes at the caudal end of the patellar ligament and at the tibial tuberosity may be associated with unresolved Osgood-Schlatter disease or an old avulsion injury with ossification formation within the patellar ligament.

MRI findings: MRI evidence of joint effusion. Osteophytes have formed along the medial and lateral articular margins of the femur and tibia, as well as along the anterior surface of the medial femoral condyle. MRI evidence of limited bone marrow edema in the region of the medial femoral condyle, as well as subchondrally in the medial tibial plateau. Presence of small subchondrally located cysts in the medial femoral condyle and in the patella. The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur on the medial half of the joint is thinned, in places lysed, to a greater degree on the femoral side. The patellar cartilage is of preserved thickness. MRI evidence of damage to the medial meniscus. In the anterior horn of the medial meniscus, a hyperintense line with a horizontal course is seen, which reaches the edge of the meniscus and extends into the body and to its posterior horn. Degenerative changes are depicted in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, in which a triangular zone of increased signal intensity is seen ("meniscus-within-meniscus sign"). Both menisci are extruded laterally, without fragment formation. MRI evidence of partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The fibers of the posterolateral bundle of the ligament are of wider cross-section and with increased signal intensity. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Patellar retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – with preserved thickness and signal characteristics. A small perisynovial cyst is seen, located dorsally, measuring 8.7/5.0 mm. A small multilocular Baker's cyst with typical location and dimensions of 13/8 mm. MRI evidence of subcutaneous edema along the anterolateral and, to a lesser degree, along the anteromedial surface of the knee joint and lower leg. Soft tissue edema around the medial collateral ligament.

Conclusion: MRI evidence of joint effusion. Medial gonarthrosis – grade II–III. Bone marrow edema with the described location. Degenerative damage in the anterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2b; damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2c. Partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Perisynovial cyst. Multilocular Baker's cyst. Soft tissue and subcutaneous edema.

TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable apart from very subtle increased signal seen in the proximal patellar tendon laterally. There is associated focal edema seen within Hoffa's fat pad inferior to the lateral aspect of the lower pole of patella also involving the lateral edge of the patellar tendon. Findings are consistent with mild lateral patellar tendinosis. Edema in Hoffa's fat may be associated with extensor mechanism impingement.

There is focal signal change and irregularity of the articular cartilage of the medial facet of patella consistent with moderate chondrosis. The remainder of the articular cartilage of patella is well-maintained. The trochlear articular cartilage is also reasonably preserved.

The TT-TG distance measures about 1 cm, within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus appears intact with no surfacing tear demonstrated. Immediately adjacent to the posterior horn of medial meniscus tracking along the joint margin posteriorly from the posterior root attachment medially to the medial joint margin deep to the semimembranosus and semitendinosus tendons there is a large multiloculated parameniscal cyst. This measures about 3.7 cm in length with short axis measurements of up to 1.2 x 0.9 cm.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact.

There is no Baker's cyst or knee effusion demonstrated.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Mild patellar tendinosis with edema in Hoffa's fat pad laterally. The edema may indicate presence of extensor mechanism impingement of Hoffa's fat pad.

There is a large para meniscal cyst closely associated with the posterior horn and body of medial meniscus. There is no discernible, associated medial meniscal tear identified.

No evidence of internal derangement.

MRI findings: No MRI evidence of joint effusion. The bones forming the right knee joint are of normal shape. A limited zone of bone marrow edema is seen in the medial tibial condyle. MRI evidence of an oval bone lesion located centrally in the proximal tibial diaphysis. The finding measures 6/5 mm and has typical macromorphology of an enchondroma.
The articular cartilage of the tibia and femur has preserved thickness and congruence. MRI evidence of damage in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. A hyperintense line with horizontal course is seen within it, reaching the meniscal edge without contact with the articular surfaces of the tibia and femur. MRI evidence of degenerative changes and damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. The posterior horn of the lateral meniscus shows diffusely increased signal intensity, with a hyperintense line of horizontal course also seen within it. The line does not reach the articular surfaces of the bones. Normal appearance of the anterior horn of the medial meniscus and the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus. MRI evidence of partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. It is thickened and with diffusely increased signal intensity. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. MRI evidence of total rupture of the medial collateral ligament. The ligament is traced with preserved integrity and signal intensity only in its proximal part at its femoral attachment. In its middle third it shows increased signal intensity, and distally it does not attach to the tibia. Lateral collateral ligament – unremarkable. MRI evidence of a small zone of increased signal intensity in the semimembranosus tendon. This zone is located at the insertion site of the tendon on the medial tibial condyle. Patella, patellar cartilage – unremarkable. Patellar retinacula – normal appearance. Patellar ligament and quadriceps femoris tendon – normal appearance. Popliteal fossa – unremarkable. MRI evidence of edema in the soft tissues on the medial side of the joint, as well as in the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior surface of the lower leg.
Conclusion: MRI evidence of partial rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament – grade 2. Damage in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus – grade 2a. Degenerative changes and damage in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus – grade 2c. Rupture of the medial collateral ligament. Limited zone of bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle. Soft tissue and subcutaneous edema. Tendinopathy at the insertion site of the semimembranosus muscle on the tibia. Enchondroma in the tibial diaphysis.

Technique: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

Findings:
- From the evaluation of the medial compartment, destruction of the articular cartilage is identified (mostly ICRS grade 4) with degeneration and subluxation of the medial meniscus and large marginal osteophytes. A large complex of parameniscal cysts arises from the body of the medial meniscus and extends posteriorly to the medial collateral ligament with maximum dimensions 3.4 x 2 x 3 cm (transverse x anteroposterior x craniocaudal).
- From the evaluation of the lateral compartment, degeneration of the lateral meniscus is identified, thinning of the articular cartilage (ICRS up to grade 3) and marginal osteophytes. The popliteus tendon also shows degeneration.

- Osteophytes are also observed within the intercondylar notch in combination with a complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
- Joint effusion is observed intra-articularly with the presence of loose bodies.
- Benign hypertrophy is observed in the bone marrow of the tibia and the femur.
- A small Baker's synovial cyst is seen adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

CONCLUSION
- Degenerative osteoarthritis in all compartments of the knee, particularly pronounced in the medial compartment.
- Large parameniscal cyst from the medial meniscus.
- Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
- Prepatellar bursitis.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Three-month history of nontraumatic left posterior knee pain. Ultrasound suggests medial meniscal tear. Assess for internal derangement   .

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact.

There is splitting of the fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament unassociated with thickening or deficiency. The finding is favored to represent a described but rare anatomic variant. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is intact and unremarkable.

Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint appears to be reasonably well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The medial meniscus is intact. Involving the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus there is some contour flattening of the inferior margin of the meniscus peripherally suggesting possible deficiency of a portion of the meniscotibial ligamentous attachment. There is no evidence of a significant medial meniscal tear. Articular cartilage of the medial compartment is reasonably well-maintained. There is fraying seen to the posterior surface of the weightbearing surface of medial femoral condyle consistent with moderate focal chondrosis.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament is intact. Fibers appear mildly attenuated compatible with a remote partial-thickness sprain. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Projecting in the intercondylar notch surrounding the anterior cruciate ligament, situated anterior to the posterior cruciate ligament there is a multiloculated ganglion cyst measuring about 1.9 cm in length and 1.5 x 1.3 cm in short axis. The finding is consistent with an anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

The medial collateral ligament is intact.

The lateral collateral ligament complex including the IT band, fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is no evidence of a significant Baker's cyst. A small 8 x 4 mm ganglion cyst is seen projecting posterior to the proximal tendon fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

Marrow signal is within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Moderate chondrosis to the medial joint compartment associated with contour flattening of the inferior surface of the posterior horn and posterior body of medial meniscus. This finding is equivocal but could indicate presence of partial deficiency of the meniscotibial attachment in this region. No discrete medial meniscal tear is identified.

Mild attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament consistent with remote partial thickness injury. Associated anterior cruciate ligament ganglion cyst.

Suspected congenital duplication of the medial patellar retinaculum.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The lateral meniscus is normal. The medial meniscus is extruded 3.5 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss is present in the meniscus, with grade III degeneration observed in the posterior horn and body segments. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. No joint effusion is detected. A well-defined, subcortically located lesion measuring 31x15 mm in the posterior aspect of the distal femoral metaphysis, slightly hypointense on T1 and T2-weighted images with a T2 hyperintense central area, of benign morphology not causing cortical destruction, was observed. The described lesion was primarily interpreted as a non-ossifying fibroma. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, subchondral sclerosis and irregularity on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint, and subchondral millimetric cysts and edema in the medial femoral condyle were observed. Loss of integrity in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level was observed. Findings were interpreted as degenerative arthritis. CONCLUSION: Non-ossifying fibroma of the femur, gonarthrosis, volume loss and medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and STIR. A T2 gradient echo sequence was also acquired. [DATE].

FINDINGS:
Re-evaluation of the complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
Re-evaluation of the partial injury of the upper third of the posterior cruciate ligament, showing improvement in imaging characteristics.
The foci of bone bruise that had been observed in the region of the distal femur and proximal tibia are no longer observed.
Callus formation of the fracture of the fibular head is observed with mild alteration of the superior surface (malunion).
In the lateral femoral condyle, a small bone infarct is observed, probably secondary to a previous bone bruise in the area.
In the medial femoral condyle, a small subarticular insufficiency fracture is observed (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis") with extensive bone edema. Bone densitometry of the lumbar spine is recommended.
The articular surfaces are evaluated as intact.
Mild tendinopathy is observed in the superior portion of the patellar tendon.

[BILATERAL NOTE: two reports filed under this study]

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T2, T2 me2d, and PD FS sequences.

FINDINGS:
- Blurring of the proximal fibers of both cruciate ligaments is noted, in the context of complete tears. The probability of a few intact fibers is considered low.
- Diffuse pathological signal with accompanying blurring of the proximal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament is recognized, in the context of a partial tear, while there is coexisting morphological thinning at its midportion, possibly in the context of a morphological tear.
- Numerous areas of pathological bone marrow signal are observed in both the femoral and tibial condyles, in the context of residual bone edema. A microtrabecular fracture is noted in the lateral femoral condyle subarticularly, with a transverse dimension of ~8.5 mm.
- An avulsion fracture of the fibular head is noted with displacement up to 5 mm.
- Intense edema of the periarticular soft tissues is observed, mainly at the medial aspect, in the popliteal fossa and at the level of the gastrocnemius muscles, in the context of both the aforementioned injury as well as other postoperative procedures.
- Thickening and pathological signal are observed in the popliteus tendon.
- The menisci and articular cartilage are satisfactorily evaluated.

DIAGNOSIS:
- From the evaluation of the medial compartment, narrowing of the joint space is observed with thinning and focal full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage, in the setting of degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment.
- From the evaluation of the bone marrow, osteomedullary edema is observed in the proximal epiphysis of the tibia at the medial condyle, with an accompanying minimal microtrabecular fracture in the subchondral region, measuring 9 mm in length, in the setting of a subchondral insufficiency fracture of the knee (SIFK).
- The menisci, cruciate ligaments, and collateral ligaments appear normal.
- No pathological findings are observed from the evaluation of the extensor mechanism.
- A small joint effusion is observed intra-articularly.
- A full-thickness fissure is observed in the articular cartilage of the patella centrally.
- An ovoid intra-articular formation ~1 cm is identified anterior to the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, which could represent a cartilaginous intra-articular loose body.
- The remaining articular cartilage is within normal limits.
- Small, ill-defined bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle adjacent to the insertion of the medial head of the gastrocnemius is attributed to an avulsion injury.
- The remaining bone marrow demonstrates signal within normal limits.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Tricompartmental marginal osteophytes.

Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Moderate Baker's cyst.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. There is marked MCL bursitis.

MRI Findings:

Right knee joint: MRI findings of medial gonarthrosis. Multiple defects are seen in the articular cartilage on the medial side of the femur. The cartilage is thinned and has irregular contour outlines. Osteophytes are visualized along the femoral condyles, predominantly on the medial side. Subchondral bone marrow edema is present in the medial femoral condyle, related to the degenerative changes in the overlying cartilage. The articular cartilage on the lateral side of the joint is preserved. A degenerative change and lesion of the medial meniscus is visualized in the region of its posterior horn. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus has high signal intensity and is fragmented. Part of the meniscus is displaced laterally from the joint space. Degenerative change is also found in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, with a small (6 mm) cyst within it. Joint effusion is present. The cruciate ligaments are intact. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon, patellar ligament – unremarkable.

Left knee joint: Medial gonarthrosis is also seen in the left knee joint, which is relatively more pronounced. The articular cartilage on the medial side is almost completely lysed, with the joint space filled with fluid. Relatively larger osteophytic deposits are visualized along the femoral condyles. Small osteophytes are also found along the articular surfaces of the tibia. Subchondral bone marrow edema is present in the femur and in the tibia on the medial side. The medial meniscus is degenerated and fragmented. The lateral meniscus is relatively preserved. The cruciate ligaments and collateral ligaments are visualized. MRI findings of mucoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament. The ligament is traced along its entire length but has an increased diameter and increased signal intensity. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Joint effusion.

Conclusion: MRI findings of bilateral medial gonarthrosis, relatively more pronounced in the left knee joint. Bilateral joint effusion. Lesion of the posterior horns of the medial menisci – grade 3.

Acute traumatic knee.

Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate ligaments and lateral collateral ligament are unremarkable.
Thickening and increased signal of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex at its proximal aspect with partial loss of fiber continuity and edema of the regional soft tissues. The remaining components of the medial complex are unremarkable.
Peripheral central signal increase of the posterior horn and part of the body of the medial meniscus that does not appear to contact the articular surface, without features of a tear.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without criteria for tear.
Partial-thickness chondral defects of the lateral tibial plateau. The remaining femorotibial cartilages and the femoral trochlear cartilage are unremarkable. Partial and full-thickness chondral defects of the patella with diffuse distribution.
Mild to moderate joint effusion. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Quadriceps tendon, patellar tendon, pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are within normal limits.

Impression:
Signs of a grade II sprain of the proximal aspect of the medial ligamentous complex with regional soft tissue edema.
Superficial chondropathy of the lateral tibial plateau.
Patellar chondropathy with grade 2 and 3 lesions of diffuse distribution.
Mild to moderate joint effusion.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade II degeneration is observed in the lateral meniscus. Grade III degeneration is present in the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament, and the lateral ligament are normal. Mild fluid increase is observed around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Thinning of the patellar cartilage at the medial facet, with millimetric edema in the adjacent bone structures, was observed (Type 4 chondromalacia). Fluid increases are observed at the patellofemoral joint level. Fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Osteophytic spurs in the adjacent bone structures forming the knee joint, and joint space loss were observed. Additionally, there are focal thinning and loss of integrity in the tibial and femoral cartilages (findings of degenerative arthritis). Findings of tendinosis are present in the tendon of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle. A Baker's cyst measuring 35 x 5 mm in diameter is observed in the popliteal fossa. A subchondral millimetric cyst is observed at the level of the ACL insertion on the tibial intercondylar eminence.

text: Advanced, laterally predominant pan-gonarthrosis with lateral full-thickness chondropathy of both articular surfaces in the weight-bearing zone and subcortical bone marrow edema. Lateral meniscus extruded with mucoid fraying of the pars intermedia and especially of the anterior horn. The anterior horn root is no longer identifiable and lies frayed within the joint. No ganglion with mildly fluid-filled recessus (6/27). Partially deeper chondropathy also medially with mildly mucoid medial meniscus without discrete tear. ACL mildly mucoid and MCL with mild reactive changes, otherwise ligamentous apparatus intact. Pronounced patellofemoral osteoarthritis, predominantly at the lateral retropatellar facet and medial trochlea with focal deeper chondropathy and mildly laterally displaced patella. Mild insertional tendinopathy of the patellar tendon at the inferior pole. Moderate effusion with reactive synovitis. Suspicion of a loose body in the lateral suprapatellar recessus (9/18) as well as calcified loose bodies at the dorsomedial tibial plateau (CC 13 mm, 6/10). Baker's cyst with CC 4.3 cm.

2. Grade 2-3 injury of ACL, in favor of ACL tear. 
3. Bone contusion of distal femoral condyle and proxiaml tibia.
4. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
5. R/O Ramp lesion of medial meniscus.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and physical examination

COMPARISON:None.

CLINICAL HISTORY:Assess for anterior cruciate ligament tear left knee.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

The lateral meniscus is intact. Large radial tear posterior horn medial meniscus measuring at least 7 mm, with slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. Intrasubstance degeneration within the medial meniscal body without evidence of additional tear. The posterior root and anterior horn are intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament are intact. The fibular collateral ligament and biceps femoris tendon insertion are intact. Moderate popliteus tendinosis without tear. Iliotibial band is intact.

Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear. No patellofemoral subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Fissuring of articular cartilage central to medial femoral trochlea as well as overlying the medial patellar facet. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Trace knee joint fluid. Baker's cyst, with cyst fluid tracking distally along the medial superficial fascia of the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle consistent with cyst leakage. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration.

IMPRESSION:
1. Large radial tear posterior horn medial meniscus with medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Suspected prior tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament without patellofemoral subluxation.
3. Focal moderate chondrosis at the medial aspect of the patellofemoral compartment.
4. Leaking Baker's cyst.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a dominant horizontal oblique component. Mild extrusion. No displaced fragments.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade chondral fraying along the lateral aspect of the medial femoral condyle. No full-thickness cartilage defect.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis extends into the quadriceps continuation with mild overlying prepatellar bursitis.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

2. Mild extensor mechanism tendinosis involves the quadriceps continuation with mild prepatellar bursitis.
3. Mild patellofemoral compartment chondrosis.
4. Multilobulated ganglion extends from the proximal tibiofibular joint capsule into the adjacent popliteus and soleus muscles.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1-weighted, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
The following were observed:

1. Meniscocapsular detachment is identified in the lateral meniscus with tear of the posterior superior popliteomeniscal fascicle and the meniscofemoral ligament.

2. A bucket handle tear is observed in the medial meniscus with displacement of meniscal material into the intercondylar notch.

3. Complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

4. Complete tear of the posterior cruciate ligament with an old avulsion fracture, callused, at its insertion on the posterior surface of the tibia.

5. Edematous signal of the tibialis anterior muscle is observed, as in injury of the deep peroneal nerve.

6. Bone bruise is observed in a resolving phase (compared to the previous examination), at the medial femoral and medial tibial condyle.

7. Small loose bodies are observed intra-articularly.

8. Thinning of the articular cartilage of the lateral femoral and lateral tibial condyle is present from the previous injury.

9. Posterior to the torn posterior cruciate ligament, a ganglion cyst measuring 22x18x9 mm is identified.

text:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment, no significant pathological findings are observed.
In the medial compartment, there is a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus and extrusion of the remaining meniscal material, full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage of both the femoral condyle and the tibia over an anteroposterior diameter of at least 12 mm, mild bone marrow edema in the medial femoral condyle, and more extensive bone marrow edema in the medial tibial condyle where a low-signal area is also demonstrated on all pulse sequences, measuring 6 mm in anteroposterior diameter.
Intra-articularly, a large joint effusion is observed with focal frond-like projections of fatty composition and the presence of a large synovial fold suprapatellarly.
The ligamentous structures are intact.
A small enchondroma measuring 5 mm, of no clinical significance, is observed in the central portion of the tibial metaphysis.

CONCLUSION:
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment.
2. Trabecular insufficiency microfracture of the medial tibial condyle (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis").
3. Hydrarthrosis with small-scale development of secondary frond-like lipoma (lipoma arborescens).

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for several months.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Mild reactive subchondral bone marrow edema at the weightbearing aspect of the medial compartment near the medial joint line. Medial tibiofemoral and patellofemoral compartment marginal osteophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Moderate Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a meniscal flap at the posterior horn. Displacement of a meniscal flap into the tibiomeniscal recess. Severe meniscal body extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: High-grade articular cartilage loss of the weightbearing aspect of the joint with confluent areas of full-thickness cartilage loss at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: No tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity and diffuse low grade cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint with areas of high-grade fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Confluent full-thickness cartilage loss throughout the patella with subchondral signal changes. Diffuse high-grade articular cartilage loss of the trochlea with regions of full-thickness loss.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent meniscal pathology.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No lateral patellar tilt. Mild lateral patellar translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 18 mm, borderline elevated.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Severe patellofemoral and medial tibiofemoral compartment osteoarthritis. Complex tearing of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with dominant radial component at the posterior horn. Superior displacement of a small meniscal flap at the posterior horn-root junction. Severe meniscal extrusion.
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion. Moderate leaking Baker's cyst.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 months which began after a twisting injury. [REDACTED].
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture. Normal background marrow signal. No focal osseous lesion. Tricompartmental osteophytosis. Protuberant osteophytes extending into the femoral intercondylar notch. Inferior patellar enthesophytosis.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. 6 x 4 mm intra-articular body in the Baker's cyst. Fluid extends into the region of the pes anserinus 3 x 3 mm ossific intra-articular body at the anterolateral joint recess.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Intact.
Medial compartment cartilage: Low-grade articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing and posterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle with areas of high-grade cartilage loss and full-thickness fissuring.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the posterior horn-body junction.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage loss at the posterior lateral femoral condyle with areas of full-thickness fissuring.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse articular cartilage irregularity at the patella and trochlea with large confluent regions of full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial patellar facet and full-thickness fissuring throughout the trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): No tear.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Mild proximal patellar tendinosis.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance is 16 mm, top-normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact. Fluid tracking into the popliteus muscle sheath.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior distal thigh. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Tricompartmental osteoarthritis, worst at the patellofemoral compartment, where it is severe. Moderate knee joint effusion. Small multiloculated leaking Baker's cyst with synovitis. Intra-articular bodies at the anterolateral joint recess and in the Baker's cyst.
2.	Horizontal oblique undersurface tear at the lateral meniscus posterior horn-body junction.
3.	Joint fluid decompression into the popliteus muscle sheath with synovitis.

Normal.

None

The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

RIGHT KNEE

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the medial meniscus, and the articular cartilage in the medial and lateral compartments, no significant findings are observed.

Intra-articularly, a moderate joint effusion is observed in communication with a small Baker's synovial cyst, adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.

Degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior compartment of the knee with joint effusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Knee locking after trampoline injury. Associated swelling and buckling. Difficulty with knee flexion and extension. No prior surgery.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
The knee is imaged in borderline anterior drawer alignment. Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral femoral condyle and severe osseous contusion at the sulcus terminalis at the lateral femoral condyle. Additional reciprocal focal severe osseous contusions at the anterior medial tibial plateau, medial femoral condyle, and posterior medial tibial plateau. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Trace joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Small vertical tear at the peripheral aspect of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, compatible with a meniscal ramp lesion.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear at the posterior horn extending into the root. No extrusion. 
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High-grade partial-thickness chondrosis at the medial patellar facet. Chondral heterogeneity at the lateral patellar facet.The trochlear cartilage is preserved.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Near complete-complete tear of the more distal fibers.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Grade 1 sprain.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: Mild proximal patellar tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Mild edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 9 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle. Soft tissue edema at the posterior aspect of the knee.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings of a recent pivot shift mechanism injury, including: 
*	Near complete to complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) at its more distal fibers.
*	Small complex tear at the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.
*	Small vertical tear at the peripheral aspect of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, compatible with a meniscal ramp lesion.
*	Grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament (MCL).
*	Osteochondral impaction injury at the posterolateral femoral condyle, severe osseous contusion at the sulcus terminalis of the lateral femoral condyle, and additional reciprocal severe contusions at the anterior medial tibial plateau, medial femoral condyle, and posterior medial tibial plateau.

2.	Patellofemoral chondrosis with findings suggestive of active lateral patellofemoral maltracking.
3.	Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Central-marginal osteophyte formation was observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and degenerative millimetric cysts were observed on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint. Cartilage destruction was observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level. Findings were interpreted as degenerative arthritis. The medial meniscus is completely extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint. Decrease in meniscal volume, grade III degeneration, and complex tears are observed in the meniscus. The lateral meniscus is extruded 5 mm laterally from the knee joint space. Loss of integrity was observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. Grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn. The anterior cruciate ligament is markedly thinned and shows increased signal on PD images. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema was observed in the medial collateral ligament. Periarticular loose body formations, the largest measuring 7 mm in diameter, were observed in the lateral tibiofemoral joint. The tibiofibular joint space is narrowed, and subchondral cysts were observed in the lateral tibial plateau and fibular head adjacent to the joint. A Baker's cyst measuring 7x2 cm was observed in the popliteal fossa. Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue. Fluid increase was observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Extrusion from the joint space, volume loss, grade III degeneration, and complex tears in the medial and lateral menisci. Near-complete large tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Suprapatellar bursitis. Synovitis of the knee joint. Arthrosis of the tibiofibular joint. Periarticular loose body formations in the anterior tibiofemoral joint. Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa. Subchondral bone marrow edema in the patella.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    R knee injury during Muay Thai grappling   .

PRIOR IMAGING: Right knee views from [Date]
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

Extensor mechanism is intact and appears unremarkable. Patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained.

The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

There is an extensive bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus. The torn meniscal fragment occupies the intercondylar notch of the femur, adjacent to the posterior cruciate ligament creating a double posterior cruciate ligament sign. The anterior horn is anteriorly extruded. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained with mild fraying seen at the weightbearing surface in keeping with moderate chondrosis.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex are all intact.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a large knee effusion demonstrated.

Arising at the posterior meniscal root of medial meniscus extending laterally behind the posterior cruciate ligament there is a multiloculated ganglion cyst measuring 1.2 cm in height 1.7 cm in width and 0.7 cm in short axis. The finding is consistent with a meniscal/parameniscal cyst.

There is edema and soft tissue stranding in the popliteal fossa

INTERPRETATION: 

Bucket-handle tear of medial meniscus associated with moderate articular chondrosis to the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle. Associated meniscal/parameniscal cyst arising at the posterior root of medial meniscus.

Large knee effusion.
