Interpretation:

There is a small but significant intra-articular effusion. There is no Baker's cyst.

The medial meniscus is intact and without tear.

There is mild thickening of the medial collateral ligament involving, in particular, the proximal superficial fibers, associated with mild surrounding edema, consistent with a grade 1 sprain. There is a small area of edema at the posteromedial aspect of the medial femoral condyle suggesting a small associated bone contusion.

There is mild diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment with a high-grade, full-thickness chondral fissure at the junction of the weight-bearing and non-weight-bearing surfaces of the medial femoral condyle, associated with reactive subchondral changes.

There is a small oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. There is no displaced meniscal fragment.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact and without tear.

There is moderate attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with a full-thickness chondral fissure on the femoral side and associated reactive subchondral changes.

Additionally, there is a subchondral trabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau with significant associated bone edema extending anteriorly and medially. There is no associated depression of the cartilage surface.

There is thickening and more marked increased signal of the anterior cruciate ligament at its mid and proximal portions, suggesting an intermediate-grade sprain/partial tear. There is also a mild low-grade interstitial longitudinal delamination/tear of the mid and proximal fibers of the posterior cruciate ligament. There is no evidence of full-thickness involvement of the cruciate ligaments.

Patellofemoral alignment is preserved. There is mild to moderate attenuation of the patellofemoral cartilage surfaces with a full-thickness chondral fissure at the junction of the patellar apex and the lateral patellar facet, as well as along the lateral trochlea, with a focus of associated reactive subchondral changes.

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact and without tear.

Conclusion:

There is a subchondral trabecular impaction fracture at the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau, without depression of the articular surface. There is significant associated bone edema as detailed above.

There is a grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament with a small associated bone contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an intermediate-grade sprain/partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is a low-grade interstitial longitudinal delamination/tear of the posterior cruciate ligament. There is no full-thickness involvement of the cruciate ligaments.

There is a small oblique tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus. There is no displaced meniscal fragment.

There is a small intra-articular effusion.

There is no patellar fracture.

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
The medial meniscus shows simple degeneration without findings of tear.
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the extensor mechanism, no significant findings are observed.
The bone marrow shows benign hyperplasia.
Intra-articularly, a large fluid collection is observed with signs of synovitis as well as metaplasia of the synovial membrane with projecting villi in the suprapatellar recess at the medial aspect.
Varicose venous dilatations are identified in the posterior subcutaneous tissue.

CONCLUSION
The findings are in the differential diagnosis between inflammatory arthritis and early lipoma arborescens.
Rheumatological evaluation is recommended.

text:
Findings:

There is a moderate joint effusion with signs of synovitis.

There is no popliteal cyst.

The patella is positioned slightly high (patella alta). In addition, there is a mild lateral tilt of the patella, without evidence of subluxation.

There is mild patellar tendinopathy. There is no bursitis, but there is edema anterior to the patellar tendon extending down to the tibial tuberosity. The medial patellar retinaculum is slightly irregular. Hoffa's fat pad is normal. The suprapatellar fat pad is also normal.

There is grade 2 to 3 chondrosis of the patellofemoral cartilage.

There is a chronic tear of the medial meniscus. It involves the root of the posterior horn, which demonstrates increased signal with signs of maceration. This explains the significant extrusion of the body of the medial meniscus with intrasubstance edema. There is also mild extrusion of the anterior horn of this meniscus.

The lateral meniscus does not demonstrate any significant abnormality.

The anterior cruciate ligament does not demonstrate a tear.

The posterior cruciate ligament is normal.

The lateral ligamentous complex does not demonstrate any significant abnormality.

The medial collateral ligament is bowed due to the extrusion of the medial meniscus. It is also slightly thickened at its superior portion, consistent with a chronic sprain. There is no tear.

There is bone marrow edema at the corner of the medial tibial plateau in relation to this medial meniscus tear. There is also grade 2 to 3 chondrosis of the medial tibiofemoral compartment with joint space narrowing.

The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

Conclusion:

The main abnormality is this chronic tear of the medial meniscus. Since the root of the posterior horn is torn, there is complete extrusion of the body and mild extrusion of the anterior horn. This means that the meniscus no longer serves its function. Furthermore, there is joint space narrowing of the medial compartment with grade 2 to 3 chondrosis. There are also stress changes at the periphery of the medial tibial plateau as described above. This can obviously cause pain with walking and in the standing position. Clinical correlation is recommended.

Patella slightly alta with mild patellar tendinopathy.

Grade 2 to 3 chondrosis of the patellofemoral cartilage.

Joint effusion with synovitis.

Other observations made; see report above.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1-weighted pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
From the evaluation of the menisci, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, the articular cartilage, and the bone marrow, no significant findings are observed.

From the evaluation of the extensor mechanism, a high-riding patella is observed (Insall-Salvati index 1.7) as well as a TT-TG distance of 13 mm. The patella demonstrates lateral subluxation and Wiberg type II morphology. Within its articular cartilage, a small focus of chondrocalcinosis of no clinical significance is observed. At the lower pole of the patella and posterior to the upper portion of the patellar tendon, a small osteochondral foreign body of craniocaudal diameter 8 mm is observed. Between the aforementioned body and the lower pole of the patella and the anterior lateral femoral condyle, edema is observed.

CONCLUSION
The findings from the extensor mechanism support dysfunction with pathological patellar tracking and indications of patellar tendon impingement syndrome against the anterior lateral femoral condyle.

text: Tricompartmental degenerative joint disease of the knee, most prominent in the medial femorotibial compartment, characterized by full-thickness articular cartilage loss and degeneration, subchondral medullary fibrocystic and fibrovascular changes, and hypertrophic marginal osteophytes. The medial collateral ligament is bowed and surrounded by edema due to the mass effect of the extruded meniscus and parameniscal cyst. The medial meniscus is extruded medially by 8 mm. A full-thickness tear is present at the posterior root with up to 13 mm of retraction, along with degeneration at the posterior horn–body junction and irregularity at the free edge suggesting a fraying-type tear. A parameniscal cyst is observed at the anterior horn–body junction of the medial meniscus, reaching approximately 4.2 cm in size, containing thin septations and showing leakage. The lateral meniscus is normal. The quadriceps and infrapatellar fat pads are edematous. Mild tendinosis and paratenon edema are present at the proximal patellar tendon. The extensor mechanism is otherwise intact.

Interpretation:

Moderate intra-articular effusion. No significant Baker's cyst.

There is a slightly complex tear of the medial meniscus with a vertical/radial peripheral component of the posterior horn with a possible associated RAMP lesion at the meniscocapsular junction. There is an oblique longitudinal component extending to the junction with the meniscal body. Minimal extrusion of the meniscal body.

There is mild edema surrounding the medial collateral ligament consistent with a grade 1 sprain. There is mild to moderate diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment with small marginal osteophytes. There is a minimal focus of edema on the medial aspect of the medial femoral condyle, probably contusive in nature. No full-thickness defect or reactive subchondral change.

Small ganglion cysts at the origin of the gastrocnemii.

The lateral meniscus and the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear. Mild diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with small marginal osteophytes. No full-thickness defect.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact without tear. There is suspicion of a full-thickness tear, probably of the mid-distal portion of the anterior cruciate ligament, with probably associated contusion on the posterior aspect of the lateral and medial tibial plateaus.

Patellofemoral alignment is preserved.

Small enthesophytes at the distal insertion of the quadriceps with mild tendinosis/enthesopathy. No tear. The patellar tendon is intact without tear.

There is mild to moderate attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment with focal areas of grade 4 chondropathy along the medial patellar facet and the medial trochlea with full-thickness fissures and minimal associated reactive subchondral changes. Small marginal osteophytes.

Conclusion:

Full-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament with probably residual associated contusion of the posterior portion of the lateral and medial tibial plateaus.

Complex tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a vertical/radial peripheral component with a possible associated RAMP lesion at the meniscocapsular junction as well as an oblique longitudinal component extending to the meniscal body.

Diffuse tricompartmental grade 1-2 chondropathy with focal areas of grade 4 chondropathy on the medial aspect of the patellofemoral compartment.

Moderate intra-articular effusion.

Other findings as described above.

TECHNIQUE: PD sequences with fat suppression, T1 and T2* were performed.

FINDINGS:
- Moderate amount of intra-articular fluid with extension into the suprapatellar recess and the lateral gutters. Within the suprapatellar recess, a horizontal membranous fold is visualized.
- A popliteal (Baker's) cyst is identified adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius with a craniocaudal length of approximately 5.4 cm.
- Diffusely abnormal signal and discontinuity at the posterior root, with associated subluxation of the medial meniscus.
- The ligamentous structures have normal appearance.
- Edematous appearance of the prepatellar space.
- On evaluation of the articular cartilage, full-thickness loss is identified at the medial articular surface of the patella (ICRS stage 4). Full-thickness loss is also identified at the dependent portion of the medial femoral condyle with a width of approximately 6 mm and associated edema of the underlying bone marrow (ICRS 4).
- On evaluation of the posteromedial corner, abnormal signal is identified at the insertion of the semimembranosus muscle, consistent with tendinopathy.

CONCLUSION:
1. Findings of osteoarthritis of the medial and anterior compartments with moderate amount of intra-articular fluid and Baker's cyst.
2. Tear of the posterior root, degeneration and subluxation of the medial meniscus.

MRI LEFT KNEE
TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.
FINDINGS
A degenerative tear is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with subluxation thereof.
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, the cruciate and collateral ligaments, and the extensor mechanism, no significant findings are observed.
On evaluation of the bone marrow, extensive osteomyelitic edema is observed in the medial metaphysis of the proximal tibia with the presence of a subarticular low signal intensity lesion on all pulse sequences, thin, measuring 12 mm in length.
At the same level, erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade III is observed in the medial femoral and medial tibial condyle.
A moderate fluid collection is observed in the knee joint in communication with a Baker's synovial cyst in the medial popliteal fossa.
CONCLUSION
Findings consistent with insufficiency fracture (synonymous with "spontaneous osteonecrosis") in the medial proximal epiphysis of the proximal tibia.
The articular surface is intact.
There is coexisting joint effusion and degenerative tear of the medial meniscus.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
- The anterior cruciate ligament shows a complete chronic tear at its proximal half, with myxoid degeneration of its stump.
- The posterior cruciate ligament appears normal.
- Extensive degenerative changes, with full-thickness cartilage defects, osteophytosis, and subarticular bone marrow edema, are observed in the medial compartment of the knee.
- The medial meniscus shows a horizontal degenerative tear of the body and posterior horn with subluxation.
- Full-thickness fissures are observed in the articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea with subarticular osteomedullary edema as well as small marginal osteophytes.
- Minimal thinning is present in the cartilage of the lateral compartment of the knee. The lateral meniscus shows degeneration without a definite tear.
- A Baker's cyst with craniocaudal length of up to 4.1 cm is observed adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle, with minimal fluid infiltration of the soft tissues around its edges, indicative of rupture.
- The bone marrow and the collateral ligaments appear within normal limits.
- No evidence of extensor mechanism dysfunction is observed.
- An accessory fabella is observed in a typical position posterior to the lateral femoral condyle, as an anatomical variant.

CONCLUSION
1. Degenerative osteoarthritis of the medial compartment with degenerative meniscal tear.
2. Chronic complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

Findings of early degenerative osteoarthritis in the medial compartment.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, pd/T2 fs, and T2* pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the medial compartment, there is a degenerative complex tear and subluxation of the medial meniscus, full-thickness erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (ICRS Grade 4), as well as intense edema of the opposing surfaces of the medial femoral and tibial condyles, consistent with microtrabecular insufficiency fractures. Small marginal osteophytes are also present, one of which projects into the intercondylar notch.
- In the lateral compartment, there is a discoid meniscus which demonstrates a degenerative tear, while there is also folding of a meniscal fragment at the level of the intercondylar notch. The articular cartilage of the lateral femoral condyle shows thinning as well as chondrocalcinosis.
- On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, there is a congenitally shallow trochlea (sulcus angle 165°). Fissural erosions of the articular cartilage of the patella and of the femoral trochlea are also present.
- Intra-articularly, there is a small joint effusion and extensive synovitis with accompanying presence of numerous osteochondral loose bodies measuring 1–2 mm. Additionally, in the lateral aspect of the suprapatellar pouch, there is a projecting synovial formation measuring 1.1 cm with fat signal, which likely represents lipoma arborescens.
- The collateral ligaments and the posterior cruciate ligament appear normal. Myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament.

CONCLUSION:
1) Findings of extensive degenerative osteoarthritis in the medial compartment and early degenerative osteoarthritis in the lateral and anterior compartments.
2) Discoid lateral meniscus with a bucket-handle tear.
3) The findings of intra-articular synovitis and lipoma arborescens are attributed secondarily to degenerative osteoarthritis.
4) The findings from the extensor mechanism are consistent with patellar tracking dysfunction.

4. Bone marrow edema (bone bruise) of the medial femoral condyle.

Findings:
The medial meniscus is extruded 4 mm medially from the knee joint. Volume loss is noted in the meniscus; grade III degeneration is observed in the anterior horn, posterior horn, and body. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn, posterior horn, and body of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. Edema is observed in the prepatellar subcutaneous fat tissue. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Mild fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa. Subcutaneous varicosities are observed in the medial aspect of the crural region near the knee. Joint space narrowing is present in the medial tibiofemoral compartment; a subchondral cyst measuring up to 18x8 mm and bone marrow edema are observed in the medial tibial plateau adjacent to the joint. Loss of cartilage integrity is observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages at this level. Millimetric osteophytic spurring is present at the corners of the bony structures.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss and grade III meniscopathy, grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament, prepatellar subcutaneous edema, subcutaneous varicosities at the crural level.

text: MR Findings: Left knee joint: MR evidence of pronounced degenerative changes in the left knee joint. The articular cartilage on the medial side is completely lysed. On the lateral side, defects in the articular cartilage are seen centrally. The cartilage of the patella is relatively preserved. MR evidence of massive osteophytes along the femoral and tibial condyles. Comparatively smaller osteophytes are also visualized at the superior and inferior poles of the patella. The intercondylar eminences are sharpened. Presence of joint effusion with heterogeneous content, probably hemarthrosis. MR evidence of chronic rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact. Collateral ligaments – unremarkable. Severe degenerative changes are visualized in both menisci – the lateral meniscus shows signs of partial damage and is extruded laterally, while the medial meniscus is completely degenerated and is not visualized. Fragments of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus are visualized. Presence of subcortical bone cysts (geodes) in the medial femoral condyle and at the level of the intercondylar eminences. Calcifications in the soft tissues dorsal to the tibia are visualized. Conclusion: MR evidence of advanced gonarthrosis, more pronounced on the medial side. Degenerative changes in both menisci. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is fragmented; the lateral meniscus is extruded laterally. Chronic rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament. Joint effusion with signs of hemarthrosis. In the differential diagnosis, primary synovial chondromatosis is less likely.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, T2*, and PD fs sequences.

FINDINGS
- A large amount of intra-articular fluid is observed in the knee joint, predominantly in the suprapatellar region.
- The anterior cruciate ligament is not identified, except for a few fibers in its anterior portion. There is concurrent disorientation of the fibers of the posterior cruciate ligament, as well as deviation of the posterior femoral-tibial overlap (drawer sign) by 1.8 cm. The above findings are in favor of a (complete – subtotal) tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Clinical correlation is recommended.
- The collateral ligaments are within normal limits.
- Abnormal signal and loss of meniscal substance are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with accompanying presence of meniscal material displaced medially to the posterior cruciate ligament, measuring 1.5 x 0.5 cm, in the setting of a tear with flip.
- Full-thickness loss of articular cartilage is identified in the lateral compartment, accompanied by subchondral bone changes at the same level, in the setting of chondropathy (grade IV). Partial-thickness loss of articular cartilage is also noted in the medial facet of the patella (grade II).
- Fluid collection in the tendon sheath of the popliteus muscle, in the setting of tenosynovitis.

ACL.evidence: The anterior cruciate ligament is not identified, except for a few fibers in its anterior portion. There is concurrent disorientation of the fibers of the posterior cruciate ligament, as well as deviation of the posterior femoral-tibial overlap (drawer sign) by 1.8 cm. The above findings are in favor of a (complete – subtotal) tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

MCL.evidence: The collateral ligaments are within normal limits.

Medial Meniscus.evidence: Abnormal signal and loss of meniscal substance are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, with accompanying presence of meniscal material displaced medially to the posterior cruciate ligament, measuring 1.5 x 0.5 cm, in the setting of a tear with flip.

Lateral Meniscus.evidence: No lateral meniscus abnormality is described; however, in the setting of an acute ACL tear, lateral meniscus tears occur in approximately 20-30% of cases and the report does not explicitly exclude one.

Medial OA.evidence: No full-thickness cartilage loss is described in the medial compartment; the only medial cartilage finding is partial-thickness loss in the medial facet of the patella (grade II), which is a patellofemoral finding, not a medial tibiofemoral compartment finding.

Lateral OA.evidence: Full-thickness loss of articular cartilage is identified in the lateral compartment, accompanied by subchondral bone changes at the same level, in the setting of chondropathy (grade IV).

PF OA.evidence: Partial-thickness loss of articular cartilage is also noted in the medial facet of the patella (grade II).

Effusion.evidence: A large amount of intra-articular fluid is observed in the knee joint, predominantly in the suprapatellar region.

Synovitis.evidence: Fluid collection in the tendon sheath of the popliteus muscle, in the setting of tenosynovitis.

Baker's.evidence: No popliteal or Baker's cyst is mentioned; the fluid collection described is in the popliteus tendon sheath (tenosynovitis), which is a distinct entity from a Baker's cyst.

Contusion.evidence: Subchondral bone changes are noted in the lateral compartment but are attributed to grade IV chondropathy (degenerative), not traumatic bone marrow oedema; no discrete bone bruise is described.

Fracture.evidence: No fracture is described or suggested in the report.

text: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The medial meniscus is extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint. Grade III degeneration and an accompanying horizontal tear at the free edge are observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body of the lateral meniscus. Loss of integrity secondary to complete rupture is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The lateral collateral ligament is normal. Diffuse increase in T2 signal is observed in the posterior cruciate ligament, and grade II sprain is noted. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). A 17x13 mm extra-articular ganglion cyst is observed adjacent to the posterior superior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle. A 6.5 x 1.5 cm Baker's cyst is observed in the popliteal fossa. Subcortical degenerative millimetric cysts are observed at the attachment sites of the cruciate ligaments in the intercondylar notch of the femur and the intercondylar eminence of the tibia. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Central-marginal osteophyte formations are observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing, thinning and destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint are observed in the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Edema is observed in the subchondral area of the medial tibial plateau. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion and grade III meniscopathy of the medial meniscus, grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, anterior cruciate ligament rupture, subchondral degenerative cysts in the intercondylar notch of the femur and intercondylar eminence of the tibia, grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament, Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa, extra-articular ganglion cyst, sprain of the posterior cruciate ligament.

Clinical History:
Osteoarthritis. Pain.

Findings:
Diffuse bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle with a subcortical fracture line in the anterior weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle, without signs suggesting articular collapse. This is associated with regional soft tissue edema.
No other bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus that does not appear to contact the articular surface, without features of a tear.
The lateral meniscus is of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Thin superficial chondral ulcers of diffuse distribution in the lateral femorotibial compartment and in the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle. Trochlear cartilage without alterations. Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the lateral facet and apex of the patella.
Mild joint effusion. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon with enthesopathic changes.
Thickening and increased signal of the proximal third of the patellar tendon with enthesopathic changes, small intrasubstance tear of the central fibers involving less than 20% of the thickness and width.
Increased signal of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Bone marrow edema associated with a subcortical fracture of the anterior region of the lateral femoral condyle, without signs of articular collapse. These findings could represent phenomena of an insufficiency fracture; correlate with clinical history.
Chondropathy grade 1 and 2 lesions of the lateral femorotibial compartment and of the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle.
Chondropathy grade 2 and 3 lesions of the patella. Signs of lateral patellar hyperpressure syndrome.
Distal quadriceps and proximal patellar enthesopathic changes with a small intrasubstance tear of the proximal and central fibers of the patellar tendon.
Mild joint effusion.

Interpretation:

In the interval, there has been progression of a moderate to large intra-articular effusion with signs of chronic synovitis. There is also increase in size of a multi-lobulated, uncomplicated Baker's cyst measuring 4.4 cm in CC diameter.

There is a slightly complex tear of the medial meniscus in the interval with a probably oblique longitudinal component at the junction of the posterior horn and meniscal body with a displaced meniscal flap within the anterosuperior recess of the medial femorotibial joint space. There is moderate extrusion of the residual meniscus.

There is progression of a now severe chondropathy (grade 4) in the medial femorotibial compartment with full-thickness cartilage surface denudation and associated reactive subchondral changes. Moderate marginal osteophytes.

The medial collateral ligament is intact without tear.

Mild blunting of the free edge of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus without significant meniscal tear. Mild to moderate chondral attenuation in the lateral femorotibial compartment with partial chondral fissures consistent with grade 2 chondropathy. There is no evidence of full-thickness involvement or associated reactive subchondral changes. Moderate osteophytosis. The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact without tear. There are multiple ganglion cysts related to the myotendinous junction and popliteal recess on the posterolateral aspect of the knee.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact without tear.

The femoropatellar alignment remains within normal limits. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact without tear. There is moderate diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces, with a similar focus of grade 4 chondropathy along the medial patellar facet with full-thickness fissure and early associated reactive subchondral changes, and grade 3 at the intercondylar notch with full-thickness chondral fissure. Small marginal osteophytes.

Prepatellar and infrapatellar subcutaneous edema, nonspecific.

Conclusion:

There is a new slightly complex interval tear involving the medial meniscus with an oblique longitudinal component at the junction of the posterior horn and meniscal body and a displaced meniscal flap within the anterosuperior recess of the medial femorotibial joint space as described above.

There is progression of femorotibial chondropathy, predominantly medial, with grade 4 involvement.

Progression of an intra-articular effusion now moderate to large and of an uncomplicated Baker's cyst with associated signs of synovitis.

There is no other significant interval change including grade 4 chondropathy along the medial patellar facet.

Indication: Approximately 2 weeks of right knee pain after fall while skiing.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There are foci of bone marrow edema at the terminal sulcus of the lateral femoral condyle and posterior lateral tibial plateau consistent with a recent pivot shift type injury. No suspicious bone marrow signal abnormality is identified.

JOINT SPACE:
Alignment is anatomic. There is a small to moderate knee joint effusion. No calcified/ossified intra-articular bodies are identified. Trace Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Small focus of surfacing signal abnormality (seen best on series 4, image 21 and series 6, image 19), which may represent a small undersurface tear at the junction of the body/posterior horn of the medial meniscus. No extrusion, displaced fragment, or para meniscal cyst is identified.
Medial compartment cartilage: Slight cartilage heterogeneity and fraying along the central weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle without discrete high-grade defect. Medial tibial plateau cartilage appears intact.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Intact.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Focal, mild cartilage fraying along the posterior/central lateral tibial plateau.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Markedly edematous and enlarged with near complete/complete mid substance disruption.

MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, T2 gradient echo, and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
Evaluation of the lateral compartment reveals small marginal osteophytes as well as mild degeneration of the meniscus without tear.

In the medial compartment, significant degenerative osteoarthritis is observed with complete erosion of the articular cartilage (ICRS grade 4), degenerative tear of the meniscus and extrusion of the remaining meniscal material, presence of marginal osteophytes and subarticular bone marrow lesions on both sides.

Evaluation of the anterior compartment reveals complete erosion of the articular cartilage at the inferomedial aspect of the articular surface of the patella.

Intra-articularly, multiple loose bodies are observed posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament, as well as the presence of foci of lipoma arborescens extending into the suprapatellar recess.

Evaluation of the bone marrow reveals a benign enchondroma in the proximal tibial epiphysis.

Incidentally, enthesophytes are noted at the intercondylar notch, the largest of which is in contact with the anterior cruciate ligament, which demonstrates mucoid degeneration. Small ganglion cysts are observed in the anterior articular compartment and larger ganglion cysts posterior to the distal femoral metaphysis.

* Subcutaneous edema in distal thigh to proximal leg and intermuscular edema in the popliteal fossa.

MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    Clicking, locking, exclude meniscal tear..

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination. The extensor mechanism is intact. There is patella alta. The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.6.
The finding is associated with advanced patellofemoral joint osteoarthritic change with extensive denuding of the articular cartilage and with extensive subcortical cyst formation particularly seen along the apex and lateral facet of patella. Prominent trochlear and patellar osteophytes are demonstrated.

The medial patellar retinaculum is attenuated likely related to previous lateral dislocation and partial disruption. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact.

There is a degenerative medial meniscal tear. There is maceration and linear signal seen in the posterior horn extending into the body. An oblique inferiorly surfacing tear of the body and posterior horn is a demonstrated. The finding is associated with severe chondral denuding and exuberant marginal osteophyte formation seen to the medial joint compartment. There is also subcortical edema seen to the weightbearing surface of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau.

The lateral meniscus is macerated and not identified at the body and posterior horn. Findings are in keeping with extensive maceration and degenerative tearing of the body and the posterior horn of lateral meniscus. The finding is associated with denuding of the entire articular cartilage of lateral joint compartment associated with prominent lateral joint compartment osteophyte formation. There is also subcortical sclerosis and mild edema seen within the lateral joint compartment. An intraosseous cyst is seen to the lateral femoral condyle with 3 cm in keeping with subcortical tear.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament near its femoral insertion. There are pivot shift bone marrow contusion with a subchondral impaction fracture involving the lateral femoral condyle with associated significant bone marrow edema. There are also bone contusion involving the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau without fracture.

There is high-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament with complete disruption of its fibers at its femoral attachment with also thickening and increased signal throughout the superficial component. There is no distal avulsion or proximal retraction of the distal superficial component. There is also complete tear of the deep meniscal femoral component with significant thickening of the meniscal tibial component.

There is a horizontal tear involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending to the inferior articular surface. There is no displaced meniscal fragment. There is a an oblique tear involving the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus at the insertion of the Wrisberg ligament compatible with a Wrisberg rip.

There is edema involving the myotendinous junction of the popliteus. The popliteus tendon itself is intact.

Otherwise the posterior cruciate ligament, the extensor mechanism, the semimembranosus, the distal biceps femoris, the lateral collateral ligament and the IT band are unremarkable.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL.

2. High-grade sprain of the medial collateral ligament without evidence of pseudocyst Stener.

3. Medial and lateral meniscal tear without displaced fragment.

4. Pivot shift bone marrow contusion with subchondral impaction fracture of the lateral femoral condyle.

5. Moderate knee joint effusion.

There are intrasubstance degenerative changes involving the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is a superimposed horizontal tear. The tear extends from the posterior horn to the body. The tear extends to the inferior articular surface of the meniscus. There is no displaced fragment. There is a small parameniscal cyst adjacent to the posterior horn. The lateral meniscus demonstrates intrasubstance degenerative changes involving the body without a well-defined linear tear.

2. Intrasubstance degenerative changes of the menisci with superimposed horizontal tear of the medial meniscus as detailed above.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the lateral meniscus, articular cartilage, lateral collateral ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, and bone marrow, no pathological findings are observed.
The medial meniscus is identified with pathological signal at the body and posterior horn with vertical morphology.
The medial collateral ligament shows thickening at the femoral attachment, without edema.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows horizontalization.
On evaluation of the extensor mechanism, focal edema is observed in Hoffa's fat pad.
A small fluid collection is observed intra-articularly.

CONCLUSION:
1. Chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Vertical tear of the medial meniscus at the body and posterior horn.
3. Old healed partial injury of the medial collateral ligament.
4. The edema in Hoffa's fat pad is attributed to mild impingement syndrome of the patellar tendon against the anterior distal femur.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Acute subchondral insufficiency fracture at the weightbearing medial femoral condyle. Confluent subchondral bone marrow edema at the medial femoral condyle. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. Normal background marrow signal. Proximal patellar enthesophytes.

JOINT SPACE:
Moderate joint effusion with synovitis. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Diffuse complex degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus. Superiorly displaced meniscal flap at the medial joint line and at the posterior horn. Severe meniscal extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: Large confluent regions of full-thickness articular cartilage loss at the weightbearing aspect of the joint. High-grade cartilage loss at the posterior medial femoral condyle.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Small complex tear of the lateral meniscal body, characterized by a dominant horizontal component.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage irregularity at the weightbearing aspect of the joint without focal defect.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): No tear.

Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Periligamentous edema, likely related to adjacent pathology.

Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Extensor Apparatus: Normal quadriceps tendon. Normal patellar tendon.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No disproportionate muscle atrophy. Intramuscular edema at the popliteus and tibialis anterior, possibly reflecting low-grade strains. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar and scattered subcutaneous edema about the knee. Deep soft tissue edema at the posterior thigh. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Subchondral insufficiency fracture of the weightbearing medial femoral condyle without articular surface collapse. Mild/early subchondral insufficiency fracture at the anteromedial tibial plateau. 
2.	Moderate knee joint effusion with synovitis.
3.	Complex degenerative tearing throughout the medial meniscus with multiple displaced meniscal flaps and severe meniscal extrusion.
4.	Complex tearing of the lateral meniscal body.
5.	Tricompartmental chondrosis, severe in the medial compartment.

text: [DATE]: * MRI Right Knee 15ch AA : Clinical Information: Right knee pain. Diagnostic question: Evaluation. Scan protocol (DRB): sagittal intermediate-weighted sequences without and with fat suppression, axial/coronal PD-weighted sequences with fat suppression, coronal T1-weighted sequences. Findings: - No significant distension of the suprapatellar bursa, limited to mildly increased amount of fluid in the semimembranosus/gastrocnemius-semimembranosus bursa. - Chondromalacia of the medial femorotibial compartment with global cartilage loss as well as grade 4 cartilage defects, subchondral insufficiency fracture both tibial and femoral (with significant perilesional edema and periosteal soft tissue infiltration extending to the metaphysis). - Complex (partial to sub)total tear/maceration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (near the posterior meniscal root) with extra-articular extrusion of the body portion, also characterized by an undersurface tear and locoregional mucoid degeneration. - Grade 1 sprain pattern of the MCL, secondary to the above-described findings. Furthermore: "Full thickness" cartilage loss/denudation of the medial patellar facet and patellar ridge (extending to the lateral facet, partially undermined) - associated sharpening of the joint margins. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis (as described above) with a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus - secondary to this, subchondral insufficiency fractures of the medial femorotibial compartment.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the medial compartment, small marginal osteophytes are observed, along with thinning and microerosions of the articular cartilage of the femoral and tibial condyle (ICRS Grade II), as well as subchondral sclerosis and barely perceptible bone marrow edema of the medial tibial condyle. The medial meniscus shows extrusion and a degenerative tear of the posterior horn.
- On evaluation of the lateral compartment, no significant pathological findings are observed.
- On evaluation of the anterior (patellofemoral) compartment, a small focus of bone marrow edema is noted in the lateral facet of the patella, accompanied by complete loss of the overlying articular cartilage over a length of 9 mm (ICRS Grade IV).
- The anterior cruciate ligament shows myxoid degeneration, without tear.
- The posterior cruciate ligament and the collateral ligaments appear normal.
- Intra-articularly, a moderate joint effusion is observed with the presence of a few osteochondral loose bodies measuring up to 9 mm in diameter. The intra-articular effusion communicates with a Baker's cyst of craniocaudal diameter, within which a loose body measuring 3.5 mm in diameter is identified.
- A small enchondroma measuring 1.3 cm in diameter is observed in the tibial epiphysis.

CONCLUSION:
1) Findings indicative of degenerative osteoarthritis of the anterior and medial compartments with degenerative tear of the medial meniscus.
2) Myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament.
3) Moderate intra-articular fluid collection with osteochondral loose bodies.

text:
Findings:

Moderate intra-articular effusion, with suspicion of a fat-fluid level on the lateral side suggesting a degree of lipohemarthrosis. No significant Baker's cyst, with a thin rim of fluid within the popliteal fossa and the proximal portion of the pes anserinus.

There is blunting of the posterior margin of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, suspicious for a potential peripheral vertical longitudinal tear. There is also relatively significant extrusion of the meniscal body, most likely related to a complete tear of the medial collateral ligament.

There is a complete tear of the distal medial collateral ligament with proximal retraction of the torn fibers, associated with multiple zones of irregularity, thickening, and abnormal intrasubstance signal. There is also attenuation and intrasubstance signal at its origin. The torn distal portion of the medial collateral ligament is situated slightly beneath the pes anserinus tendons, constituting a "pseudo-Stener" type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep meniscofemoral component and a partial tear of the meniscotibial component.

No full-thickness chondral defect of the medial femorotibial compartment.

The lateral meniscus is intact without tear. There is a small fracture on the superior aspect of the fibular head, potentially at the insertion of the arcuate popliteal ligament. Minimal displacement and associated edema. The distal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament and the biceps tendon is preserved, as is the origin. There is also a small ossification on the posterior aspect of the fibular head measuring 5 mm, of indeterminate origin.

There are subchondral bone irregularities at the weight-bearing surface of the lateral femoral condyle, appearing rather chronic. No full-thickness chondral defect of the lateral femorotibial compartment. However, a small focus of edema on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with mild chondral hyperintensity, contusion versus osteochondral lesion (atypical) versus stress change related to the origin of the lateral gastrocnemius.

Ganglion cyst at the origin of both gastrocnemii.

There is a tear appearing complete at the distal insertion of the posterior cruciate ligament and/or PCL avulsion. The ligament is proximally retracted, thickened, and of abnormal signal. There is significant attenuation of the anterior cruciate ligament without a full-thickness component noted, however, consistent with a partial tear. There are contusions likely involving the lateral tibial plateau, more marked posteriorly +/- impaction/subchondral fracture.

Small ganglion cyst at the distal footprint of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Patellofemoral alignment remains within normal limits. Sequelae of Osgood-Schlatter disease with chronic-appearing fragmentation of the tibial tuberosity and mild thickening of the patellar tendon. The distal quadriceps tendon is intact without tear. No full-thickness chondral defect of the patellofemoral compartment. Hoffa's fat pad is unremarkable.

There is significant diffuse subcutaneous and intermuscular edema. There is also edema of the popliteus and plantaris muscles consistent with a sprain.

Conclusion:

Complete tear of the distal medial collateral ligament with displacement of the distal portion beneath the pes anserinus tendons, consistent with a "pseudo-Stener" type lesion. There is also a complete tear of the deep meniscofemoral component and a partial tear of the meniscotibial component.

Tear appearing complete of the distal posterior cruciate ligament and/or PCL avulsion. Probable partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.

Fracture of the superior aspect of the fibular head, probably at the insertion of the arcuate popliteal ligament. Associated edema.

Additionally, probable contusions of the lateral tibial plateau +/- impaction/subchondral fracture and of the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle.

Blunting of the posterior margin of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus, suspicious for a potential peripheral vertical longitudinal tear.

Moderate intra-articular effusion with suspected lipohemarthrosis component.

In this context, further investigation with CT is recommended to better evaluate the bony structures. Additionally, an orthopedic surgery consultation is also strongly recommended.

The report was transcribed as a priority.

Clinical History:
Left knee pain.

Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate ligaments and lateral collateral ligament are unremarkable.
Thickening with predominantly low signal of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex in its proximal third, with minimal peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle in a reactive pattern. Increased central signal of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus that may contact the inferior articular surface at the level of the body peripherally, without displacement of segments.

Mild increased signal of the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon and the proximal insertion of the patellar tendon, without signs of tear.
Pes anserinus tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band are within normal limits.

Impression:
Sequelar thickening of the superficial and deep components of the medial ligamentous complex in its proximal third, with minimal peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial femoral condyle in a reactive pattern. Edema of the adjacent soft tissues, deep to the pes anserinus tendons, may represent findings of an associated regional friction syndrome.
Probable peripheral tear of the medial meniscus, correlate clinically.
Grade 3 chondropathy of the central region of the femoral trochlea.
Edema of the suprapatellar retroquadriceps fat pad, nonspecific finding. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis and proximal patellar tendinosis.

Clinical History:
Obs. Degenerative meniscopathy.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within preserved limits. Polylobulated cystic ganglion that appears to have an intra-articular and extra-articular component in the posterior region of the knee, measuring approximately 22 x 20 mm in its largest transverse axes and approximately 28 mm in the craniocaudal axis.
Menisci appear of preserved morphology and signal, without signs of tear.
Cartilage of the femorotibial compartments and femoral trochlea without abnormalities. Nearly full-thickness degenerative chondral ulcer of the lateral facet of the patella, not displaced.
Increased signal of the superolateral aspect of Hoffa's fat pad.
Minimal joint effusion. Small polylobulated popliteal cyst, without signs of complication.
Mild increased signal of the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, without signs of tear. Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris and iliotibial band within normal limits. Soft tissue edema between the iliotibial band and the lateral femoral condyle.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1 proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
In the lateral compartment of the knee, there is simple degeneration, without tear of the meniscus.
In the medial compartment of the knee, a degenerative tear is observed in the posterior horn of the meniscus and subluxation thereof. Additionally, bone marrow edema is observed in the medial femoral condyle and epicondyle, as well as articular cartilage erosion ICRS grade III of the medial femoral condyle and epicondyle. Intra-articular fluid collection communicates with a Baker's synovial cyst with a craniocaudal diameter of 6.5 cm in the medial popliteal fossa.

CONCLUSION
The findings are consistent with an insufficiency fracture (synonymous with spontaneous osteonecrosis) of the medial femoral condyle.

Focal thinning is observed in the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint.

Interpretation:

There is a minimal rim of fluid within the suprapatellar recess, without significant intra-articular effusion. There is a small Baker's cyst, without significant complication, measuring 2.8 cm in CC diameter.

There is a horizontal longitudinal tear involving the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus, extending to the posterior root, to the junction with the anterior horn and along the inferior articular surface. There are small parameniscal cysts associated on the posterior aspect.

There is thickening of the superficial fibers of the medial collateral ligament with mild to moderate surrounding edema suggesting a grade 1 sprain.

There is mild to moderate attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment, without full-thickness involvement. There are small marginal osteophytes.

The lateral meniscus and the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact and without tear.

There is mild to moderate diffuse attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment with a focus of severe chondropathy at the non-weight-bearing surface on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle with focal full-thickness loss of the cartilage surface and early associated reactive subchondral changes. There are minimal marginal osteophytes.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact and without tear. There are minimal intraosseous ganglion cysts beneath the distal insertion of the anterior cruciate ligament.

The patellofemoral alignment appears within normal limits. There are several magnetic susceptibility artifacts on the anterior aspect of the patellar tendon, most likely of post-interventional/surgical nature; to correlate clinically.

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are grossly intact and without tear.

There is mild prepatellar thickening which could be related to sequelae of bursitis.

There is mild attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment, mainly at the trochlear surface with foci of severe chondropathy along the intercondylar notch and the lateral trochlear facet with full-thickness fissures and associated reactive subchondral changes. There are small marginal osteophytes.

There are millimetric ganglion microcysts related to the proximal tibiofibular joint.

Conclusion:

Horizontal longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus as described above with small parameniscal cysts associated on the posterior aspect.

Grade 1 sprain of the medial collateral ligament.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy with foci of severe chondropathy at the non-weight-bearing surface on the posterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and along the trochlear surface in the patellofemoral compartment.

No significant intra-articular effusion.

Small uncomplicated Baker's cyst.

MRI of left knee was performed in sagittal, axial and coronal sections.

No evidence of bone contusion is noted.

4. Suspected tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus and anterior horn of lateral meniscus.

text: MR findings: MR findings consistent with medial gonarthrosis. The articular cartilage of the femur and tibia on the medial side is thinned and has irregular contours. Presence of joint fluid at the site of the lysed cartilage. Small zones of subchondral bone marrow edema are seen in the medial condyle of the femur and tibia. A large Baker's cyst measuring 60/22 mm is seen. Degenerative changes are visualized in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. The posterior horn of this meniscus is enlarged and has increased signal intensity. Hyperintense lines are found within it, corresponding to a tear. The tear extends to the posterior edge of the meniscus and to the articular surfaces of the femur and the tibia. Degenerative changes are also found in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus, without a visible tear in it. The anterior cruciate ligament has a thinned diameter – a finding consistent with a chronic partial tear. Presence of a small zone of bone marrow edema in the tibia beneath the insertion site of the anterior cruciate ligament. The collateral ligaments are intact. Retinacula – unremarkable. Quadriceps femoris tendon and patellar ligament – normal appearance. Conclusion: MR findings consistent with medial gonarthrosis. Degenerative changes in the menisci. The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is fragmented. Chronic partial tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. Joint effusion. Baker's cyst.

FINDINGS:

There is a large knee joint effusion. There is significant soft tissue swelling surrounding the knee.

There is complete tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. There is thickening and increased signal involving the distal posterior cruciate ligament with partial tear (approximately 50% of the fibers) of the posterior medial fibers. There is mild thickening and increased signal involving the proximal and mid aspect of the PCL.

There is complete radial tear of the posterior root of the lateral meniscus. The medial meniscus is unremarkable.

There is complete tear of the medial collateral ligament with distal avulsion of the superficial component which is retracted proximally and superficial to the pes anserine tendons compatible with a pseudoStener lesion. There is also high-grade injury involving the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial component of the MCL with thickening of the posterior oblique ligament.

There is almost complete tear of the lateral collateral ligament at its femoral attachment. There are thinned out fibers that appear physically continuous. This is likely a functionally complete tear. There is also almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon as it courses around the lateral femoral condyle with significant thinning and laxity of the tendon. There is disruption of the popliteal fibular ligament. The distal biceps femoris insertion remains intact.

There is significant bone marrow edema at the posterior tibial plateau fractures. There is also bone contusion involving the anterior aspect of the lateral femoral condyle and minimal contusion at the medial femoral condyle.

There is an enchondroma in the distal femur.

CONCLUSION:

1. Complete tear of the ACL with a moderate grade injury of the PCL.

2. High-grade injury involving the medial collateral ligament including distal avulsion of the superficial MCL with pseudo Stener lesion.

3. High-grade tear of the lateral collateral ligament which is likely functionally complete.

4. Almost complete tear of the popliteus tendon. Injury to the popliteal fibular ligament.

5. Complete radial tear involving the posterior root of the lateral meniscus.

6. Significant bone marrow edema surrounding the known tibial plateau fracture with a bone contusion in the lateral femoral condyle.

7. large knee joint effusion.

Intra-articularly, a large joint effusion is observed with a large cartilaginous loose body at the lateral recess measuring 12x10 mm.

In the medial popliteal fossa, a Baker's cyst is observed with locally viscous content, craniocaudal diameter of 4 cm, and signs of microtears of its wall with presence of free fluid in the gastrocnemius bursa.

MRI  KNEE  -  LEFT

TECHNIQUE:  Unenhanced multiplanar multisequence MR images of the knee.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Fall onto left knee while downhill skiing 3 months ago. Immediate bruising. Has had residual swelling and medial joint line pain. X-ray is negative for OA. Please evaluate for meniscal or ligamentous pathology.

COMPARISON:  None.

FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout images were reviewed.

Radial tear posterior horn and adjacent posterior root of the medial meniscus with slight peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact. The lateral meniscus is intact.

ACL, PCL MCL and LCL are intact.

MCL and LCL are intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.

Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament. No patellofemoral subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits.

Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture peripheral weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle, measuring 8 mm anterior to posterior and 6 mm medial to lateral. Exuberant surrounding marrow edema. No evidence of displaced 1 stable osteochondral fragment.

Focal fissuring of articular cartilage central weightbearing aspect medial femoral condyle as well as central to medial femoral trochlea and along the patellar apex and medial patellar facet.

Incidental finding 0.8 x 1.1 x 1.3 cm lowT1 signal intensity and high T2 signal intensity lesion, likely to represent an enchondroma.

3.5 x 1.3 x 2.7 cm the Baker's cyst. Trace fluid in the pes anserine bursa.

Small volume joint effusion.

INTERPRETATION:

1. Radial tear posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus slight extrusion. 
2. Nonspecific subchondral insufficiency fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.
3. Medial femorotibial and patellofemoral chondrosis most pronounced involving the patellofemoral compartment suggesting evolving mild patellofemoral predominant osteoarthritis of the left knee. 
4. Low-grade partial thickness tear of the medial patellofemoral ligament without patellofemoral subluxation. 
5. Mild pes anserine bursitis.
6. Incidental finding of enchondroma.

An edematous appearance is present in the subcutaneous fat tissue surrounding the knee joint. Narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral joint space, subchondral edema, and cartilage thinning were observed. An appearance consistent with a Baker's cyst with septations and lobulated contours, measuring 76x20 mm, is present in the popliteal fossa.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo sequences.

FINDINGS
- Extensive bone marrow edema is observed in the medial femoral condyle and on the medial tibial plateau, with a subarticular low-signal lesion on all sequences. A similar, smaller lesion is observed in the medial tibial condyle. There is only subtle flattening of the articular surface of the medial femoral condyle. The remaining articular surfaces are intact.
- Abnormal signal is observed in the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with contour abnormality and subluxation.
- Osteoarthritis is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage of the medial femoral condyle and medial tibial plateau, as well as with the presence of osteophytes. Early osteoarthritis is observed in the lateral patellofemoral compartment.
- Thickening and abnormal signal of the medial collateral ligament at its midportion and toward its femoral insertion, likely reactive to the displacement of the medial meniscus.
- Moderate amount of intra-articular fluid with mild synovitis.

CONCLUSION
1. Findings consistent with insufficiency fracture of the medial femoral and tibial condyles (synonym: "spontaneous osteonecrosis").
2. Degenerative tear of the medial meniscus with joint effusion.

Findings:  Small knee joint effusion. No intra-articular loose bodies. No sinister bone marrow changes.  10 mm x 6 mm by 16mm well-defined lobulated intramedullary lesion in the distal metadiaphysis of the right femur display low signal on T1 and high signal on PD sequences. Multiple hypointense foci within the lesion representing calcification. No perilesional edema, endosteal scalloping or cortical destruction. Findings are in keeping with a low-grade chondroid lesion (enchondroma).  Intact cruciate and collateral ligaments.  Intact lateral meniscus. Radial tearing of the inner free of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the distal biceps femoris tendon, popliteus tendon, pes anserine tendons and distal iliotibial band.  Intact quadriceps and patellar tendons. Severe patellofemoral degenerative changes with high-grade chondral thinning and full-thickness chondral loss along the lateral retropatellar facet and corresponding lateral femoral trochlea surface with underlying stress changes. The patella is lateralized relative to the femoral trochlear groove. Evidence of trochlear dysplasia with a shallow trochlear groove.  Relatively well-maintained medial and lateral tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage. Tricompartmental osteophyte formation noted.  
Conclusion:  Radial tearing of the inner free edge of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus. Severe patellofemoral degenerative changes with evidence of trochlear dysplasia and lateralization of the patella relative to the trochlear groove.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with right knee pain to the lateral joint line and infrapatellar pain after injury. Rule out meniscal tear.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanism is intact. There is prepatellar edema which may correlate clinically with prepatellar bursitis.

 The Insall Salvati ratio measures about 1.4 consistent with mild patella alta. There is some attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum with slight lateral subluxation of the patella. Findings may relate to remote injury related to transient lateral dislocation of the patella.

There is chondral fissuring and chondral loss seen to the patellar apex and lateral facet associated with subcortical cyst formation in the patella and with edema. The articular cartilage of the femoral trochlea demonstrates mild chondral fissuring seen at the trochlear apex but is otherwise reasonably well-maintained. The TT TG distance measures about 9 mm, within normal limits.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The medial meniscus contains some mild non-surfacing signal in the posterior horn and body but demonstrates no surfacing meniscal tear.

The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is reasonably well-maintained.

The anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and lateral collateral ligament complex including IT band, fibular collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and biceps femoris tendon all appear intact and unremarkable.

There is a multiloculated ganglion cyst seen within the popliteal fossa posterior to the posterior cruciate ligament. This measures 2.9 cm in height, and 1.1 by 0.8 cm in short axis. It is situated anterior to the lateral fibers of the medial head of the gastrocnemius.

There is no significant Baker's cyst. There is no evidence of significant knee effusion.

Marrow signal is otherwise within normal limits.

INTERPRETATION: 

Patella alta.

Severe chondromalacia patella. Associated attenuation of the medial patellar retinaculum, possibly related to remote transient lateral patellar dislocation.

Prepatellar bursitis.

Popliteal fossa ganglion cyst as described.

No evidence of internal derangement.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed on a 3T field strength MRI system. Evaluation was carried out with PD/fs and T1 signal intensity sequences in three planes.

Areas of benign red marrow hyperplasia are observed in the metaphyseal-diaphyseal region of the bones. No bone marrow edema is observed. Subcutaneous edema is noted around the joint, more prominently prepatellar. Suprapatellar, an ossification measuring 8 mm in longitudinal diameter is observed within the quadriceps tendon.

There is a small intra-articular effusion without a significant popliteal cyst.

text:
Clinical History:
Chondromalacia of the patella.

Findings:
No significant bone marrow signal abnormalities.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Increased central signal of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus contacting the inferior articular surface peripherally, consistent with a non-displaced tear.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of diffuse distribution in the femorotibial compartments with full-thickness ulcers of the central region of the weight-bearing zone of the medial femoral condyle.
Mild peripheral osteophytes.
Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the trochlear cartilage of diffuse distribution. Focal partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the patella with a focal full-thickness chondral ulcer of the lateral facet with secondary bone changes.
Mild joint effusion. No signs of synovitis. No pathological popliteal cysts.
Distal quadriceps and proximal patellar enthesopathic changes.
Pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris tendon, and iliotibial band within normal limits.

Impression:
Findings suggestive of a peripheral tear of the medial meniscus, degenerative, non-displaced.

Joint space narrowing is present in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, with subchondral sclerosis in the medial tibial plateau adjacent to the joint. TECHNIQUE
Sections were obtained in T1 and T2/PD sequences in three planes.

FINDINGS
- Diffusely abnormal signal within the fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament, without discontinuity, consistent with myxoid degeneration.
- Degeneration of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus (grade II). An oblique tear extending to the tibial surface is noted at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. A small radial tear at the body–anterior horn junction of the lateral meniscus.
- Thinning of the cartilage at the medial portion of the lateral tibial plateau, with a small subchondral lesion measuring 2.7 mm, with accompanying bone edema.
- Small intra-articular fluid collection with two foci of thickened synovium between the medial meniscus–medial collateral ligament and medial femoral condyle, and between the lateral meniscus and iliotibial band–lateral femoral condyle.
- The extensor mechanism and the patellofemoral joint appear normal.

CONCLUSION

The examination was performed with T1 and proton density pulse sequences with fat signal suppression.

Clinical History:
Patellar subluxation. Medial meniscopathy.
Findings:
No significant bone marrow alterations.
Cruciate and collateral ligaments within normal limits.
Marginal amputation of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
Complex tear with a main longitudinal component of the anterior horn, body, and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with a displaced "bucket-handle" segment into the intercondylar region. The remnant at the level of the body and posterior horn also shows an oblique horizontal tear contacting the inferior articular surface peripherally with minimal peripheral bone marrow edema of the medial tibial plateau in a reactive manner.
Focal linear full-thickness chondral ulcers of the central region of the lateral tibial plateau.
Superficial chondropathy of the remaining femorotibial cartilages. Full-thickness chondral ulcer of the central region of the femoral trochlea with secondary bone changes. Partial-thickness chondral ulcers of the patellar cartilage with diffuse distribution.
Moderate joint effusion. Popliteal cyst with signs of rupture with perifascial fluid extending cephalad and caudad.
Mild increased signal at the distal insertion of the quadriceps tendon, without signs of tear. Patellar tendon, pes anserine tendons, biceps femoris, and iliotibial band within normal limits.
Impression:
Complex tear of the medial meniscus with displaced "bucket-handle" segment. Tear of the remnant at the level of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus, peripheral. Mild peripheral bone marrow edema of the tibial plateau in a reactive manner.
Marginal rotation of the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus.
Chondropathy with focal grade 4 lesions of the central region of the lateral tibial plateau. Superficial chondropathy of the remaining femorotibial cartilages.
Chondropathy with grade 4 lesions of the femoral trochlea. Chondropathy with grade 1 and 2 lesions of the patella.
Moderate joint effusion. Popliteal cyst with signs of rupture.
Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: One-week history knee pain status post fall.
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. Osseous contusion along the peripheral lateral femoral condyle, no superimposed fracture. Background marrow signal is otherwise normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Mild partial-thickness fissuring at the median ridge, no superimposed shearing injury/delamination. No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: High grade tearing involving the medial patellofemoral ligament at the femoral attachment with extensive surrounding soft tissue edema and blood products.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Findings compatible with recent transient patellar dislocation compatible characterized by moderate osseous contusion involving the peripheral lateral femoral condyle and high-grade tearing involving the MPFL at the femoral attachment.
2.	Mild patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, no superimposed posttraumatic shearing/delaminating defect.

text: RIGHT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: Grade III degeneration and a meniscal root tear were observed in the medial meniscus. The medial meniscus appears extruded medially. Periligamentous edema is present around the medial collateral ligament (grade I sprain). Grade II degeneration was observed in the lateral meniscus. The anterior cruciate ligament signal is diffusely increased, with focal thinning and irregularity in caliber proximally and distally (complete rupture). The posterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament are normal. Focal cartilage thinning at the medial facet level of the patellar cartilage and a subchondral millimetric cyst in the adjacent bone were observed (grade II chondromalacia). Mild osteophytic spurring in the bony structures forming the knee joint, joint space narrowing in the medial tibiofemoral compartment, and significant cartilage thinning were observed (findings of degenerative arthritis). Focal subchondral bone marrow edema at the level of the medial tibial plateau and diffuse bone marrow edema at the level of the medial femoral condyle were observed. Millimetric cysts at the level of the tibial intercondylar tubercle and lateral plateau with mild surrounding bone marrow edema were observed. A lobulated-contoured Baker's cyst measuring 8x8 mm was observed in the popliteal fossa. Peritendinous cysts were observed around the semitendinosus, gracilis, and semimembranosus tendons. A cystic lesion measuring 24x10 mm was observed at the inferior posterior level of the tibiofibular joint (ganglion cyst). Signal increase consistent with grade I-II strain in the popliteus muscle and a cyst approximately 1 cm in diameter at this level were observed.

text:
MRI OF THE RIGHT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with pulse sequences: proton density with fat signal suppression and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS
- On evaluation of the menisci, simple degeneration is observed without evidence of tear.
- The ligamentous structures are intact.
- On evaluation of the articular cartilage, no findings are observed in the medial and lateral compartments. Degeneration is observed in the articular cartilage at the medial surface of the patella (ICRS III). Coexisting degenerative changes are present in the subcortical bone marrow at the mid-portion of the patella.
- A small fluid collection is observed intra-articularly with features of synovitis.
- A small Baker's synovial cyst is observed adjacent to the medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle.
- Small ganglion cysts are observed at the tibiofibular junction.
- Small osteophytes are observed in the region of the intercondylar notch arising from the medial femoral condyle, as well as at the inferior pole of the patella.
- Suprapatellar edema is observed in the corresponding fat pad, which has a craniocaudal diameter of 2.5 cm.

CONCLUSION:
Findings of degenerative osteoarthritis at the patellofemoral joint, with findings particularly at the medial articular surface of the patella, with accompanying effusion and mild synovitis. The edema of the suprapatellar fat pad could be attributed to impingement of the quadriceps tendon against the femoral bone in the context of the aforementioned osteoarthritis.
