On a series of native sections through the left knee, moderate degenerative changes of the femorotibial joint are seen in the medial compartment. Zones of erosion and grade IV chondromalacia of the cartilage with a zone of bone edema in the area of the medial femoral condyle.
Adequate visualization of the patellofemoral joint with normal signal intensity of the cartilage of the corresponding articular surfaces.
Zone of bone edema posteriorly in the area of the medial tibial condyle.
Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in the middle third.
Atypical appearance and depression in the area of the lateral tubercle of the intercondylar eminence at the insertion site of the anterior cruciate ligament with free bone fragments – status after avulsion fracture?

The medial meniscus shows altered signal intensity with a complex tear of the body and posterior horn and discontinuity of the posterior meniscal root. Small parameniscal cysts adjacent to the anterior horn. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 4 mm with consequent distension of the medial collateral ligament, without signs of rupture.
Rupture of the anterior intermeniscal ligament.
The lateral meniscus shows appropriate signal intensity, without signs of rupture.
Mild enthesopathic changes at the proximal insertion of the lateral collateral ligament.
Enthesopathic changes of the popliteus tendon.
Normal appearance of the iliotibial tract and pes anserinus.
Enthesopathic changes at the insertion of the quadriceps tendon and at both insertions of the patellar ligament.
Patellar retinacula are intact.
Moderate amount of joint effusion, most pronounced medially.
Mild edema of the soft tissues medially.
Baker's cyst measuring approximately 14 mm in length.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: osteoarthritis
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 3.0 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
No joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Degeneration involving the posterior horn/body of the medial meniscus without discrete tear by MR criteria.

Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Mildly edematous.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Mildly edematous.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. There is a lateral patellar translation.. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology.  

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
There is a minimal edema noted anterior to the patellar tendon. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1. Mildly edematous medial patellar retinaculum, nonspecific and can be seen with mild sprain.
2. Degeneration of the medial meniscus without obvious tear.
3. Minimally edematous MCL, could be related to grade 1 sprain.

text:
- The study reveals evidence of lateral part of right fibular head fracture with the bony fragment dislocated, measuring about 1.3 cm from the fracture site and measured in size about 1.2xintact9xintact9 cm in APxWtxHt dimensions. This fracture fragment is seen attaching to the arcuate ligament without evidence of disruption of the arcuate ligament. Overall findings are suggestive for avulsion fracture of the right fibular. head. 
 - There is associated mild high SI along distal part of lateral collateral ligament, distal part of biceps femoris tendon and also at the conjoined tendon at the fibular attachment; suggested strain. 
 - High marrow SI at anterior aspect of proximal tibia and posterior aspect of medial femoral condyle is demonstrated; suggested bone contusion. 
  
 Central supporting system  
 - Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Abnormal orientation with high grade partial thickness tear at distal part of ACL with high SI along entire ACL. The tear is located about 6 mm above the medial eminence.  
 - Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): High grade partial thickness tear at mid to distal part of PCL is shown. No evidence of avulsion at tibial attachment site. 
 - Anterior tibial translation: None.  
  
 Medial compartment  
 - Medial meniscus: High SI at meniscofemoral and meniscotibial region; suggested meniscocapsular injury. 
 - Medial collateral ligament: High SI at deep band of medial collateral ligament; suggested strain. 
 - Medial tibial plateau, medial femoral condyle: Preserved chondral cartilage. 
  
 Lateral compartment  
 - Lateral meniscus: Several tears as described; 
 -- Horizontal high SI along anterior horn of lateral meniscus; suggested horizontal tear. 
 -- Vertical high SI at anterior horn of lateral meniscus; suggested combined vertical tear. 
 -- Radial tear at posterior horn of lateral meniscus with involvement of the posterior root. 
 - Iliotibial band: Normal.  
 - Lateral collateral ligament and biceps femoris tendon: Mild high SI along distal part of lateral collateral ligament, distal part of biceps femoris tendon and also at the conjoined tendon at the fibular attachment; suggested strain. 
 - Popliteus tendon: Poorly identified course of the popliteus tendon with high SI at the myotendinous junction; suggested partial tear of the popliteus tendon. Intermediate SI of the popliteus muscle is shown; suggested muscle strain. 
 - Popliteofibular ligament: Preserved, normal alignment.  
 - Lateral tibial plateau, lateral femoral condyle: Preserved chondral cartilage. 
  
 Patellofemoral compartment  
 - Focal bone marrow edema at the inferior part of the patella bone. 
 - Quadriceps tendon: Normal.  
 - Patellar ligament: Normal.  
 - Medial patellar retinaculum: High SI with some part thinning at the attachment to medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL); suggested medial patellar retinaculum strain with partial tear of MPFL. 
 - Lateral patellar retinaculum: Normal.  
 - Moderate amount of hyperintense SI fluid causing distension of the suprapatellar bursa. Mild thickening of the synovial tissue is noted. 
 - Moderate fat stranding at the suprapatellar fossa is shown. 
 - Normal articular cartilage of patellar facet and femoral troclear is observed.  
  
 Others  
 - Subcutaneous edema extending from prepatellar to tibial tuberosity region. 
 - Subcutaneous contusion along posteromedial, anteromedial, posterolateral and anterolateral aspect of subcutaneous layer is shown. 
 - Superficial fluid along fascia is seen. 
 - Hyper SI at distal part of tibialis posterior, vastus intermedius and vastus medialis muscle are seen; suggested muscle strain. 
 - A fat globule anterior to the proximal tibia is shown. 
 - Visualized neurovascular bundles show intraluminal eccentric loss of flow void at the popliteal vein with dilatation distally; suggested deep venous thrombosis. The popliteal artery is grossly preserved. - Avulsion fracture of lateral part of right fibular head with associated strain of lateral collateral ligament and bicpes femoris tendon. 
 - Partial tear of popliteus tendon. 
 - Horizontal and vertical tear at anterior horn of lateral meniscus. Radial tear at posterior horn with posterior root tear of lateral meniscus. 
 - Meniscofemoral and meniscotibial tear. 
 - Medial patellar retinaculum strain with partial tear of MPFL. 
 - High grade partial thickness tear at distal part of ACL. 
 - High grade partial thickness tear at mid to distal part of PCL. 
 - Bone contusion at anterior aspect of proximal tibia and posterior aspect of medial femoral condyle with soft tissue contusion at posteromedial, anteromedial, posterolateral and anterolateral aspect of knee joint. 
 - Deep venous thrombosis at right popliteal vein.

MRI RIGHT KNEE:

INDICATION:    5 weeks ago patient felt popping sensation in the right knee during rotation motion. Able to weight-bear at the time of injury and presently tenderness at fibular head. Difficulty flexing the past 90 degrees. Ultrasound revealed effusion with synovial thickening and positive McMurray's test for medial aspect in clinic.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There are no normal intact fibers of the anterior cruciate ligament in keeping with a complete mid fiber tear of the anterior cruciate ligament. The finding is associated with an anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment of about 8 mm. There is evidence of resolving bone contusions in the anterior lateral femoral condyle with slightly depressed anterior sulcus and resolving bone contusions in the posterior lateral tibial plateau. Findings are consistent with resolving kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is also edema in the posterior aspect of the medial tibial plateau.

Buckling of the posterior cruciate ligament is noted in association with the anterior tibial drawer. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

The medial collateral ligament is intact. There is some mild intrinsic signal around the deep fibers of the medial collateral ligament in keeping with a low-grade medial collateral ligament sprain.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact including the fibular collateral ligament, biceps femoris tendon, the popliteus tendon and the IT band.

There is an undisplaced vertical tear of the peripheral one third of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the posterior aspect of the posterior body. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment are well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact and unremarkable. The patellofemoral ligaments are intact and unremarkable. Articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is well-maintained. The TT-TG distance is within normal limits.

There is no significant Baker's cyst or significant knee effusion. There is mild reactive synovitis within the joint.

INTERPRETATION: 

Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear of mid fibers associated with a significant anterior tibial drawer.

Resolving kissing bone contusions in association with pivot shift mechanism of injury.

Low-grade sprain of the medial fibers of medial collateral ligament.

Undisplaced radial tear of peripheral one third of posterior horn of medial meniscus extending into posterior body.

text: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The medial meniscus is extruded 5 mm medially from the knee joint space. Volume loss, maceration, and complex tears are observed in the meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior and posterior horns and body segment of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. The posterior cruciate ligament, lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps tendons are normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. A Baker's cyst measuring 7.5 x 3 cm is observed in the popliteal fossa. Edema in the subchondral area and cartilage thinning are observed in the lateral facet of the patella. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing, mild subchondral sclerosis, edema, and millimetric cysts are observed in the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint in the medial tibiofemoral compartment. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilages is observed at this level. CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis, medial extrusion of the medial meniscus, volume loss, maceration, and complex tears, grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus, myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament, suprapatellar bursitis, synovitis of the knee joint, Baker's cyst in the popliteal fossa, grade III chondromalacia of the lateral facet of the patella.

Clinical History:
Severe osteoarthritis.

Findings:
No diffuse bone marrow signal abnormalities.
ACL continuous, increased in caliber, with diffuse signal alteration suggestive of mucoid degeneration.
PCL and collateral ligaments without significant abnormalities.
Medial meniscus of normal morphology, with complex degenerative tear of the posterior horn, with an oblique longitudinal component extending from the posterior root.
The lateral meniscus shows a large complete radial tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body, with a large meniscal defect, associated with maceration and fibrillation of the remnants.
Diffuse full-thickness chondral thinning in the lateral femorotibial compartment, with foci of subchondral bone edema. Signal alteration and diffuse superficial irregularity of the cartilage in the medial femorotibial compartment, with areas of subtotal and full-thickness thinning in the non-weight-bearing posterosuperior region of the femoral condyle, with a subtle focus of subchondral bone edema.
Increased signal and moderate diffuse chondral thinning of the patellar cartilage. Diffuse irregularity of the trochlear cartilage, with areas of thinning and fine subtotal and full-thickness ulcers on the inferior aspect of both facets.
Marginal femorotibial osteophytes with lateral predominance and patellofemoral osteophytes.
Marked joint effusion, with prominent chronic synovial proliferation. Small posterior capsular cystic ganglia in the midline.
Quadriceps, patellar, popliteus, semimembranosus, biceps femoris, iliotibial band, and pes anserine tendons of normal thickness and signal.
Muscle groups with preserved trophism.

Complete radial tear at the junction of the posterior horn and body of the lateral meniscus, with a large meniscal defect and marked degenerative changes of the remnant.
Complex degenerative tear of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
Advanced degenerative changes of the lateral femorotibial compartment. Diffuse medial femorotibial chondropathy grade 1-2, with small grade 3 lesions on the femoral condyle.
Patellofemoral chondropathy grade 3-4.
Marked joint effusion and chronic synovitis.
Signs of mucoid degeneration of the ACL.

MRI LEFT KNEE

TECHNIQUE
The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

FINDINGS
On evaluation of the medial compartment, a degenerative tear of the medial meniscus is observed, in the presence of marginal osteophytes, erosion of the articular cartilage at the femoral and tibial condyles ICRS grade III, subarticular bone marrow edema on both sides of the joint space, and accompanying joint effusion. The findings are consistent with degenerative osteoarthritis.

In the lateral compartment of the knee, no significant findings are observed.

On evaluation of the anterior compartment, mild degenerative changes are observed with lateral marginal osteophytes on the patella and femoral trochlea, but without cartilage erosion. Intra-articularly, fluid collection is noted which contains small structures of fatty tissue. The finding corresponds to lipoma arborescens. The bone marrow shows benign hyperplasia.

In the popliteal fossa, a venous aneurysm is observed approximately 8 cm in length.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Complete avulsion of the biceps femoris from the fibular head associated with a large multiloculated soft tissue hematoma surrounding the tear extending along the lateral gastrocnemius muscle.
Complete avulsion of the popliteus tendon at its insertion on the lateral femoral condyle.
Severe edema and irregularity of the lateral collateral ligament proper with high-grade partial-thickness tear from its femoral attachment and complete avulsion from its fibular attachment.

Normal.

Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Diffuse edema of the visualized proximal anterior compartment of the leg muscles. Associated diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection.

None

6.Osteochondral impaction fracture of the medial femoral condyle/trochlea associated with underlying bone marrow reactive changes/contusions.
7.Diffuse thickening and increased signal intensity of the common peroneal nerve suggesting low-grade traumatic injury without fiber discontinuity or transection. Associated denervation edema of the visualized anterior muscle compartment of the proximal leg.

text:
MRI LEFT KNEE:

INDICATION:    [Age] female with trauma during ski accident 1.5 weeks ago with persistent pain, swelling and limited range of motion of left knee.

PRIOR IMAGING: None.
.
TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

There is a complete tear of the midportion of the anterior cruciate ligament. No normal intact fibers are identified. There is a borderline anterior tibial drawer measured in the lateral joint compartment at about 5 mm. There are bone contusions seen at the lateral femoral sulcus in the posterior aspect of the lateral tibial plateau consistent with kissing contusions related to a pivot shift mechanism of injury. There is a discrete region of linear low T1 signal along the posterior rim of the lateral tibial plateau which may indicate presence of an undisplaced lateral tibial plateau rim fracture.

The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

There is abnormal signal surrounding the medial collateral ligament at its origin along its course proximal to the medial joint line consistent with grade 2 sprain. There is significant disruption of the deep fibers with intact superficial fibers extending distally. The posterior oblique ligament appears intact. There is an associated partial thickness sprain of the femoral insertion of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

The lateral collateral ligament complex is intact. There is some subtle increased signal seen in the proximal fibers of the fibular collateral ligament which could indicate presence of a low-grade sprain. The fibular collateral ligament, IT band, biceps femoris tendon and popliteus tendon appear intact.

There is abnormal increased T2 signal seen in the periphery of the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body consistent with a meniscocapsular avulsion injury. No discrete surfacing meniscal tear is identified to the medial meniscus. The articular cartilage of the medial joint compartment is well-maintained.

The lateral meniscus is intact. The articular cartilage of the lateral joint compartment is well-maintained.

The extensor mechanism is intact. The lateral patellofemoral ligament is unremarkable. As noted the medial patellofemoral ligament at its femoral insertion demonstrates a partial thickness sprain. The articular cartilage of the patellofemoral joint is reasonably well-maintained apart from some mild fissuring seen to the trochlear articular cartilage at the apex and involving the medial facet. Findings are consistent with moderate chondrosis.

No significant Baker's cyst is demonstrated.

There is a moderate to large knee effusion.

INTERPRETATION:
 
Complete anterior cruciate ligament tear with bone contusions corresponding to a pivot shift mechanism of injury and with possible undisplaced posterior tibial plateau fracturing. Plain film correlation is recommended.

Grade 2 medial collateral ligament sprain associated with partial-thickness sprain of the insertional fibers of the medial patellofemoral ligament.

Evidence of meniscocapsular injury to the medial meniscus involving posterior horn and body with no discrete surfacing tear identified.

Moderate chondromalacia patella.

Moderate knee effusion.

Minimal rim of fluid within the suprapatellar recess without significant intra-articular effusion. Multi-lobulated and elongated Baker's cyst extending up to 8 cm in CC diameter. No evidence of complication or sign of rupture.

Chronic-appearing horizontal longitudinal tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.

Mild chondropathy in the medial and lateral femorotibial compartments.

Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Multifocal areas of subchondral edema along the lateral tibial plateau and femoral condyles.

Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

Edema of the popliteus muscle. No muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

Moderate joint effusion with synovitis as well as subchondral marrow edema along both tibial plateau and femoral condyles and edema of the posterolateral corner. Findings are concerning for early inflammatory arthritis, for which aspiration should be considered.

Osteophytic changes in the bony structures forming the knee joint, with narrowing of the joint space particularly medially and subchondral sclerosis, are observed (findings of degenerative arthritis).

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 pulse sequences, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo.

FINDINGS:

The findings are attributed to a microtrabecular insufficiency fracture (synonym of "spontaneous osteonecrosis"). There is coexisting reactive edema of the medial collateral ligament. A similar lesion, of lesser extent, is observed in the lateral portion, near the midline, of the tibial epiphysis. Increased amount of intra-articular fluid is noted. The lateral meniscus is depicted with diffusely increased signal in the setting of a degenerative tear. The medial meniscus is depicted subluxated, with diffusely increased signal mainly in the posterior horn and body in the setting of a degenerative tear. A few erosions of the patellofemoral joint are observed with mild thinning of the cartilage at the same level in the setting of early osteoarthritis. The cruciate ligaments and the lateral collateral ligament appear normal.

On evaluation of the medial compartment, degeneration of the meniscus without tear is observed, presence of osteophytes, and mild erosion of the articular cartilage. On evaluation of the anterior compartment, lateral subluxation of the patella is observed with erosion of the articular cartilage ICRS grade 4 at the lateral articular surface and presence of subchondral bone marrow lesions. Intra-articularly, joint effusion is observed with presence of small cartilaginous loose bodies. In the intercondylar notch, osteophytic formations are observed accompanied by myxoid degeneration of the anterior cruciate ligament secondary to impingement syndrome. Additionally, on evaluation of the articular cartilage, extensive chondrocalcinosis is observed in the context of CPPD.
Conclusion: Degenerative osteoarthritis of the lateral and anterior compartments.

text: LEFT KNEE MRI. Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence. Findings: The lateral meniscus and medial menisci are extruded from the joint space with significant volume loss, maceration, and grade III degeneration observed in the menisci. Loss of continuity secondary to complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament is observed. The posterior cruciate ligament has a markedly buckled appearance. Central-marginal osteophyte formation is observed in all three compartments of the knee joint. Joint space narrowing in the medial and lateral tibiofemoral compartments, subchondral sclerosis, edema, and millimetric cysts on the bone surfaces adjacent to the joint are observed. Destruction of the femoral and tibial cartilage is observed at this level. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. Ossified nodular lesions, the largest measuring 7 mm in diameter, surrounded by synovial fluid are observed posterior to the knee joint, adjacent to the popliteus tendon sheath. Findings are interpreted in favor of synovial chondromatosis. A tear in the posterosuperior aspect of the knee joint capsule with an associated 2.5x1.5 cm ganglion cyst is observed. A 3x2 cm extra-articular ganglion cyst is observed posterior to the knee joint. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Anterior subluxation of the tibia from the tibiofibular joint is observed. The cartilage on the lateral facet of the patella is markedly thinned. Conclusion: Gonarthrosis. Extrusion, volume loss, maceration, and grade IIII meniscopathy in the medial and lateral menisci. Complete rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament and buckled appearance of the posterior cruciate ligament. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Tear of the posterior knee joint capsule and associated ganglion cysts. Suprapatellar bursitis and synovitis of the knee joint. Subluxation of the tibia. Grade II chondromalacia of the lateral facet of the patella.

The posterior horn of the medial meniscus is extruded medially from the knee joint, partially elevating the medial collateral ligament. Presence of discrete edematous changes in the subcutaneous tissue of the anterior surface of the lower leg and knee. PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the left knee according to routine protocol.

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

There is a complex fluid collection within the prepatellar soft tissues, measuring 35 x 6 x 25 mm with internal hypodensity/T2 signal as well as a thick low proton density/low T2 signal rim (measuring 4 mm in thickness). The appearance is consistent with complex prepatellar bursitis. No other discrete mass lesion identified. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

The medial meniscus shows intrasubstance degeneration of the posterior horn without discrete tear. The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 13 mm, within normal limits.

There is fissuring and thinning of articular cartilage overlying the medial patellar facet. Preserved medial and lateral femorotibial articular cartilage.

Low proton density/low T2 signal lesion within the anterior aspect of the medial femoral condyle measuring 23 x 9 x 9 mm without aggressive imaging features, likely representing a bone island.

Small knee joint effusion. Regional musculature is within normal limits. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex prepatellar bursitis, with a thick walled, 56 x 6 x 25 mm collection noted in the prepatellar soft tissues.
2. Mild to moderate patellofemoral chondrosis.

The examination was performed with T1, proton density with fat signal suppression, and T2 gradient echo pulse sequences.

The bone contusion that had been observed on the previous examination at the lateral tibial condyle is no longer seen.
The articular cartilage has normal appearance.
The anterior cruciate ligament shows thinning at its proximal and distal thirds.

CONCLUSION:
1. Partial chronic tear of the anterior cruciate ligament.
2. Joint effusion and Baker's cyst.
3. Medial meniscus tear.

Fluid:
Moderate joint effusion. Large Baker's cyst measuring up to 6.3 cm with associated fluid inferiorly along the medial gastrocnemius suggesting a partial leak.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
There is a mildly complex tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus extending to the anterior horn with a longitudinal horizontal and radial components and a flap meniscal tear probably originating from the posterior horn, displaced posteriorly and superiorly at the level of the posterior horn posterior root junction. There is also a second flap meniscal tear at the level of the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line with a displaced flap anterosuperiorly. Please see key images. There is some radial tearing at the level of the posterior root. There is significant extrusion of the meniscal body/anterior horn junction with maceration.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
The lateral meniscus and lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear.

Normal. Para ligament ganglion cysts. Underlying intraosseous ganglion cysts.

Bones:
Normal otherwise.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
None

CONCLUSION:
Potentially unstable complex medial meniscal tear with longitudinal and radial components and flap meniscal tears with displaced flap posteriorly and superiorly at the level of the posterior horn posterior root junction and anterosuperiorly at the level of the superior gutter at the medial tibiofemoral joint line. Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy, severe at the medial tibiofemoral compartment and moderate to severe at the patellofemoral compartment as detailed above.

TECHNIQUE: The examination was performed with T1 and PD sequences with fat signal suppression.

FINDINGS
- A significant amount of joint effusion is identified, with accompanying synovitis.
- On evaluation of the anterior compartment, chondral lesions of the patella are observed, without erosion of the underlying bone (ICRS 3). The infrapatellar Hoffa's fat pad shows pathological signal, while in the same anatomical region 4 nodular formations are identified, the largest measuring 1.8 cm in diameter, which contain cortex and bone marrow.
- Evaluation of the medial compartment revealed chondral lesions of the femoral condyle (up to ICRS 3 focally). Subarticular cysts are noted in the posterior aspect of both femoral condyles with accompanying bone marrow edema. Additionally, marginal osteophytes are noted on both sides of the femoral condyles as well as in the intercondylar notch, which do not, however, cause significant narrowing of it. The cruciate ligaments are normal. Degenerative changes, without tear, are observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.
- No pathological findings were noted on evaluation of the posterior compartment.

CONCLUSION
- Findings of early osteoarthritis in the setting of inflammatory arthritis.
- Nodular formations in Hoffa's fat pad, most likely representing secondary synovial osteochondromatosis.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings:
The medial meniscus is extruded 6 mm medially from the knee joint space. Grade III degeneration is observed in the posterior horn and body of the meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the anterior horn, posterior horn, and body of the lateral meniscus. Signal change secondary to myxoid degeneration is observed in the anterior cruciate ligament. Periligamentous edema is observed in the medial collateral ligament. The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are normal. The patella is normally positioned. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and knee joint space. Osteophytic spurring is observed at the corners of the bony structures at the tibiofemoral joint level. Narrowing of the joint space in the medial tibiofemoral joint, and thinning of the femoral and tibial cartilages adjacent to the joint are observed. Additionally, mild destruction is observed in some areas. Findings are interpreted in favor of degenerative arthritis. A multiseptated ganglion cyst measuring 3x2.5 cm is observed posterior to the tibiofemoral joint, in the posterior vicinity of the posterior cruciate ligament. Signal change consistent with tendinosis is observed in the tendon at the proximal insertion level of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Mild increased fluid is observed in the suprapatellar bursa.
CONCLUSION: Gonarthrosis. Medial extrusion and grade III meniscopathy of the medial meniscus. Grade II meniscopathy of the lateral meniscus. Grade I sprain of the medial collateral ligament. Periarticular ganglion cyst at the tibiofemoral joint level. Tendinosis of the medial head of the gastrocnemius. Mild suprapatellar bursitis.

TECHNICAL INFORMATION AND PROTOCOL:

Proton density and T2 weighted sagittal, coronal and axial imaging was performed through the knee including a 3D Fat suppressed proton density weighted sequence. No contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

The 3-D proton density sequence was reformatted and manipulated to aid in the interpretation of this examination.

The extensor mechanisms are intact. The patellar cartilage is intact. The trochlear cartilage is intact. The patellar soft tissues are normal.

The TT-TG interval measures 10 mm, within normal limits.

The anterior cruciate, posterior cruciate, medial collateral and lateral collateral stabilizers, including the fibular collateral collateral ligament, piriformis, biceps femoris and iliotibial tendons, appear intact. No measurable anterior tibial translation.

Medial and lateral menisci are intact. Articular cartilage of the medial and lateral femoral condyle are intact.

Small knee joint effusion. No Baker's cyst.

Bone marrow ill-defined T2 hyperintense signal within the medial patella, femoral trochlea apex and posterior medial rim.

INTERPRETATION: 
No evidence of anterior cruciate ligament injury. Medial and lateral menisci are intact. 

Bone marrow T2 signal changes of the patella and lateral femur suggestive of osseous contusion, however chondromalacia cannot be excluded. Short-term interval follow-up MRI Knee in 6 weeks could differentiate between these 2 entities. Also, clinical correlation regarding a history of direct trauma.

RIGHT KNEE MRI.
Examination protocol: Multiplanar, multisequence.
Findings: Grade I degeneration is observed in the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus. Grade II degeneration is observed in the posterior horn of the medial meniscus. There is mild diffuse signal increase in the anterior cruciate ligament. An appearance compatible with a partial tear is observed in the proximal portion of the posterior cruciate ligament. The lateral and medial collateral ligaments are normal. The distal quadriceps tendon is normal. There is no retinacular discontinuity. Fissure lines are observed in places on the medial facet of the patellar cartilage, with subchondral bone marrow edema in the adjacent bone (grade IV chondromalacia). Mild narrowing is observed in the tibiofibular joint and patellofemoral joint space. Fluid increase is observed in the suprapatellar bursa and at the level of the knee joint. The subcutaneous fatty tissue at the prepatellar level at the knee joint appears edematous. A Baker's cyst measuring up to 12 mm at its thickest point is observed in the popliteal fossa.

Diminutive posterior root and posterior horn of the medial meniscus consistent with complex tear. Displaced 6 x 6 x 6 mm meniscal fragment adjacent to the posterior root. There is peripheral extrusion of the medial meniscal body. The anterior horn is intact.

Intrasubstance degeneration of the anterior root of the lateral meniscus without discrete lateral meniscal tear.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the anterior cruciate ligament involving the posterior lateral bundle. The anteromedial bundle is intact. No tibial translation. The posterior cruciate ligament is intact.

Low-grade partial-thickness tears of the superficial medial collateral ligament as well as deep medial collateral ligament and posterior oblique ligament. Mild fluid accumulation within the pes anserine bursa.

Popliteus tendinosis without tear. The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Attenuated appearance of the medial patellofemoral ligament suggestive of prior tear. Mild lateral patellar subluxation. The lateral patellar retinaculum is intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 8 mm, within normal limits. The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

There is generalized thinning of patellofemoral articular cartilage. There is mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis. There is a nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral insufficiency fracture involving the weightbearing aspect of the medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Small Baker's cyst. Regional musculature is within normal limits.

6. Popliteus tendinosis without tear.
7. Tricompartment chondrosis consistent with mild-to-moderate tricompartment osteoarthritis of the left knee.
8. Nondisplaced 10 x 5 mm subchondral fracture medial femoral condyle with exuberant surrounding marrow edema.

text:
Interpretation:

There is a small intra-articular effusion with signs of chronic synovitis. There is also a Baker's cyst associated with synovial proliferation/chronic synovitis extending approximately 5 cm in CC diameter. This extends into the semimembranosus and pes anserinus bursae with a likely associated bursitis component.

There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial tear at the junction of the posterior root and posterior horn, and a horizontal longitudinal tear involving the residual posterior horn, meniscal body, and extending to the junction with the anterior horn. There is associated marked extrusion of the meniscal body. Additionally, there is a slightly heterogeneous and predominantly hypointense ovoid structure located intimately with the posterior margin of the posterior root of the medial meniscus measuring 7 x 14 x 7 mm. The appearance is more in favor of an intra-articular loose body that could be partially ossified versus a meniscal ossicle (less likely). The appearance is less in favor of a meniscal flap, whose signal remains slightly different from the meniscus and without demonstrated continuity with the posterior horn.

The medial collateral ligament is intact without tear. There is moderate attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the medial femorotibial compartment with full-thickness defect at the weight-bearing surfaces and small marginal osteophytes. No associated reactive subchondral change.

The lateral meniscus as well as the lateral collateral ligament complex are intact without tear.

Mild diffuse attenuation of the cartilage surfaces in the lateral femorotibial compartment, more marked at the weight-bearing surface. Small marginal osteophytes.

The anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments are intact without tear. Small pariligamentous ganglion cyst.

The patellofemoral alignment is preserved. The distal quadriceps tendon is intact without tear. Mild patellar tendinosis without tear.

Moderate attenuation of the chondral surfaces in the patellofemoral compartment with partial chondral fissure along the patellar articular surface and full-thickness defect along the trochlear surface. No associated reactive subchondral change. Small marginal osteophytes.

Conclusion:

Complex tear of the medial meniscus with a full-thickness radial component at the junction of the posterior horn and posterior root with significant extrusion of the meniscal body secondarily, and additionally, a horizontal longitudinal tear of the residual posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus extending to the junction with the anterior horn.

Tricompartmental degenerative changes/chondropathy, grade 3 involving the medial femorotibial and patellofemoral compartments and grade 1 involving the lateral femorotibial compartment.

Small intra-articular effusion and Baker's cyst with signs of associated chronic synovitis. Semimembranosus and pes anserinus bursitis with also associated chronic-appearing synovitis.

Intra-articular loose body potentially partially ossified at the posterior margin of the posterior root of the medial meniscus. A meniscal ossicle appears less likely. The appearance is less in favor of a meniscal flap, with a signal different from the meniscus and without continuity noted with the posterior horn of the medial meniscus.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Left knee pain for 2 weeks. No known cause.
Comparison: Left knee radiograph dated [DATE]

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions. Large T1/T2 hypointense, cortically based lesion along the distal medial femoral diaphysis with a slightly broader zone of transition in expected, likely represents an old nonossifying fibroma.

JOINT SPACE:
Large joint effusion with increased T1 signal compatible with hemarthrosis, with extensive synovial proliferation, including more focal focal synovitis at the posterosuperior joint space. No intra-articular bodies. No Baker's cyst.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Cartilage thinning, heterogeneity, and fissuring along weightbearing medial femoral condyle tibial plateau.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: High grade partial thickness cartilage loss along the medial patellar facet with focal high grade fissuring.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Mild distal quadriceps insertional tendinosis. No tendon tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 15 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
1.	Sclerotic cortically based lesion along the distal medial femoral diaphysis, likely representing a healed (ossified) nonossifying fibroma. Follow-up radiographs in 3 months recommended to demonstrate stability.
2.	Large knee joint hemarthrosis with extensive synovitis. Given no significant traumatic injury, differential considerations includes pigmented villonodular synovitis (PVNS), coagulopathy, infectious/inflammatory etiologies such as an inflammatory arthropathy or Lyme' s disease.
3.	Medial and patellofemoral compartment chondrosis, as described above.

MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Mild bone marrow edema and cystic changes are present at the tibial spines and at the lateral femoral condyle centrally bordering on the intercondylar notch.. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

Small joint effusion. Mild, diffuse synovial proliferation. Moderate Baker cyst.

Medial compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and surface irregularity diffusely. Small osteophytes.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: There is a complex tear involving the anterior and posterior root attachments. Fraying of the inner margin diffusely. No extrusion.
Lateral compartment cartilage: There is mild cartilage thinning at the posterior aspect, with cartilage fissuring centrally near the intercondylar notch.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: There is mild to moderate cartilage thinning and fissuring at the patella, medial greater than lateral. Trochlear cartilage appears intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.

Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 6 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.
